item.title: Senior Government Affairs Manager
item.description: Overview The Washington State and Global Employee Engagement (WSGEE) team is seeking a Senior Government Affairs Manager to work in a fast-paced environment to provide programmatic support, policy and advocacy strategy execution, government affairs outreach, and project management. This individual will be a critical member of the team, working cross-functionally across our government, community, and employee engagement teams to support our home state and the Cascadia region (WA, OR, BC) as a whole. The position will work closely with the Senior Director of Government Affairs, as well as other members of the WSGEE team, providing political and strategic analysis and recommendations that inform and execute our advocacy strategy, policy positioning, and relationship development. This opportunity will allow you to deepen and grow Microsoft’s partnerships and influence with elected and appointed officials with an emphasis on state and local officials across Washington state. You will play a key role in ensuring the government affairs team within WSGEE stays coordinated and aligned on policy positions and priority areas of work. In this role you will be a systems-thinker and proactive problem solver, creative, motivated, and personable, capable of building strong relationships and juggling multiple priorities, with a strong drive for results and commitment to excellence. You will research government affairs issues impacting business strategy and economic development, attend meetings and events, develop prep materials, and collaborate with internal teams on cross-team projects. Responsibilities Promote Microsoft as a critical force for good across issues that are imperative to a strong state economy in Washington and the Cascadia region, including housing, education, transportation, sustainability, and economic development, and a leader in technological innovation that helps people, governments and organizations achieve more. Represent Microsoft by attending, managing and coordinating events with elected and appointed officials, advocates, and other community leaders, which will involve developing content, drafting materials, and driving social media engagement. Collaborate with other teams to ensure a communications strategy is in place. Manage tracking and monitoring for policy-, industry-, or geographical-related issues and execute on Microsoft strategies and/or programs related to government affairs. Respond to issues by engaging relevant parties, prioritizing issues, sharing political intelligence, and escalating matters or contacting a subject matter experts, as appropriate. Contribute to the formation of Microsoft’s policy agenda, advocacy strategies, community relations, and/or business objectives across the company. Gather and integrate data and intelligence to support the preparation of advocacy materials, internal and external briefings, and other documentation. Lead, coordinate, and gain buy-in for intra- and cross-group projects, working with others to resolve conflicts and ensuring team alignment. Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to understand and align objectives, priorities, and resources. Qualifications Required/minimum qualifications Bachelor's Degree in Public Policy, Public Administration, Political Science, Business Administration, Technology, Law, Liberal Arts, Engineering, or related field AND 4+ years work experience in government affairs, corporate affairs, public policy, government, or related area OR equivalent experience. Additional or preferred qualifications 3+ years experience in developing and managing strategic relationships to advocate and influence public, regulatory, and technology policy priorities. 3+ years experience influencing, developing, or supporting public policy or political campaigns. Government Affairs IC4 - The typical base pay range for this role across the U.S. is USD $105,800 - $204,000 per year. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $138,400 - $223,300 per year. Certain roles may be eligible for benefits and other compensation. Find additional benefits and pay information here: https://careers.microsoft.com/us/en/us-corporate-pay This position will be open for a minimum of 5 days, with applications accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled. Microsoft is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, citizenship, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, immigration status, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran or military status, race, ethnicity, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable local laws, regulations and ordinances. If you need assistance with religious accommodations and/or a reasonable accommodation due to a disability during the application process, read more about requesting accommodations.

item.title: Director Of Congressional Policy
item.description: Description Director/Sr. Director of Congressional Policy The Director/Senior Director of Congressional Policy sits on Red Cat’s policy and strategy team and supports the Company’s advocacy at the U.S. federal level in Washington, D.C. This individual will be based in Washington, D.C. and is responsible for Red Cat’s engagement with members of Congress and their staff, as well as with Appropriations, Armed Services, Homeland Security, Oversight, and other relevant Committees. This individual will be responsible for securing Congressional appropriations for the company and identifying new Congressional appropriations opportunities. The Director of Congressional Policy will work with members of Congress and their offices to drive policy and rulemaking in the interests of Red Cat and the U.S. drone manufacturing industry. This will include shaping legislation including defense and homeland security appropriations, the National Defense Authorization Act, Community Project Funding requests, and other relevant programs and bills. This individual will also be responsible for leading and managing the Red Cat Political Action Committee. In addition, the Director will assist in covering Red Cat’s portfolio of SLTT policy priorities in the United States. This may include managing, shaping, and supporting legislation related to federal, state, and local grant programs, port security and drone for first responder (DFR) policies, domestic regulatory/rulemaking efforts, and other legislative programs of interest to the company. The Director also helps the Vice President with Red Cat policy meetings, prioritizing agenda items, background materials, and meeting follow-up items. The Director will also coordinate with Red Cat subsidiaries to build relationships with and engage relevant district members. ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS Prepare memoranda on legislation of interest to Red Cat leadership on bill introductions, hearings, mark-ups, floor action, etc. SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES SALARY RANGE MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS Education and Experience: Four years or more of progressive experience in a legislative policy position on Capitol Hill, with preference for portfolios or committee assignments covering Armed Services, Appropriations, Intelligence, and/or Homeland Security. Qualifications: Background Check This position will requ i re successfully completing a post-offer background check. Qualified candidates with a criminal history will be considered and are not automatically disqualified, consistent with federal and state law. EEO and ITAR/EAR Work Authorization Disclosure Red Cat Holdings provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. This position requires direct or indirect access to hardware, software, technology or technical data controlled under the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Successful candidates for positions subject to ITAR/EAR restrictions must provide proof of U.S. Citizenship or Permanent Residence and must not require sponsorship for export-restricted work authorization. E-Verify The company participates E-Verify ensure eligibility for employment and compliance with Right to Work rules. Compensation: Salary plus generous annual equity package and potential bonuses.

item.title: Legislative Attorney
item.description: $74,000 - $92,000 USD yearly Job ID: 37502 - Legislative Attorney Agency: Legislative Research Council Location:Pierre, SD Closing Date: Open Until Filled This is a full-time position with the Legislative Research Council, in Pierre, SD. For more information on the Legislative Research Council, please visit the LRC website . The Legislative Research Council, which is the nonpartisan research and support staff to the South Dakota State Legislature, is accepting applications for a permanent, full-time Legislative Attorney . An applicant must have an interest in the legislative process and be results-oriented, honest, discrete, trustworthy, and articulate. Duties and Responsibilities: A Legislative Attorney will assist legislators by providing accurate, objective, and relevant research information, informed by a professional understanding of the law. The significant duties include: Compiling data and conducting general and legal research for legislative committees and individual legislators and presenting alternative solutions for their consideration; Conferring with and advising legislators on legislative legal questions; Drafting and editing bills, resolutions, and amendments to implement legislators' ideas; Staffing standing committees of the South Dakota Legislature during legislative sessions, consulting with committee chairs to develop agendas and obtain testimony, and preparing committee reports; Staffing interim committees, consulting with committee chairs to develop agendas, assisting with meeting arrangements, preparing background materials, and preparing final reports; Reviewing administrative rules for form, style, clarity, and compliance with statutory authority; and Researching and writing issue memoranda and developing other resources on selected topics for review and use by the Legislature, Legislative Research Council staff, and the public. Minimum Qualifications: A Juris Doctorate from an ABA-accredited law school; An active license in good standing with the State Bar of South Dakota, or the ability to become eligible for and become admitted to the State Bar of South Dakota within one year after employment; and The ability to remain objective and nonpartisan in relation to all legislative matters, maintain confidentiality, and handle politically sensitive work. Preferred Qualifications: Very strong writing skills; Strong research and analytical skills; A willingness to develop expertise in various subject areas; The ability to communicate, both orally and in writing, in a manner that clearly and efficiently conveys information to legislators and the public; and The ability to work under tight deadlines and extended hours during the legislative session. Salary Range: For an entry level Legislative Attorney, the annual salary will range from $74,000 to $92,000. For a Senior Legislative Attorney with previous related experience, the annual salary will range from $88,000 to $130,000. The actual starting salary will depend on qualifications and experience. Application Process: This position will remain open until filled. This position is exempt from the Civil Service Act and is employed at will. Any application or resume submitted for consideration will be kept confidential. Applications, consisting of a letter of interest and resume, should be submitted online ( https://gen-stateofsouthdako-trn.inforcloudsuite.com/hcm/xmlhttp/shorturl.do?key=4TP ) or e-mail to: South Dakota Legislative Research Council 500 East Capitol Avenue, Pierre, SD 57501 E-Mail: Legis.Resume@sdlegislature.gov | Phone: 605-773-3251 Pierre, South Dakota, United States $74,000 - $92,000 USD yearly

item.description: Job Requisition ID: 58717 Opening Date: 09/16/2026 Closing Date: 09/30/2026 Agency: Department of Revenue Class Title: ADMIN ASSISTANT I - 00501 Skill Option: None Bilingual Option: None Salary: Anticipated Starting Salary $5,834 - $7,100 monthly Job Type: Salaried Category: Full Time Number of Vacancies: 1 Bargaining Unit Code: None Merit Comp Code: Confidential (Management Bill) Exclusion from RC028 Collective Bargaining Coverage Work Hours: Monday - Friday; 8:30am - 5pm Anticipated Hybrid Work Schedule Availability: Not available, fully in office Headquarter Location: 101 W Jefferson St, Springfield, Illinois, 62702 Work County: Sangamon Agency Contact: Brent.Stice@illinois.gov A resume is highly encouraged to evaluate your qualifications and skills as part of your application. Please attach a DETAILED Resume/Curriculum Vitae (CV) to the MY DOCUMENTS section of your application if you decide to provide one. Why Work for Illinois? Working with the State of Illinois is a testament to the values of compassion, equity, and dedication that define our state. Whether you’re helping to improve schools, protect our natural resources, or support families in need, you’re part of something bigger—something that touches the lives of every person who calls Illinois home. No matter what state career you’re looking for, we offer jobs that fit your life and your schedule—flexible jobs that provide the gold standard of benefits. Our employees can take advantage of various avenues to advance their careers and realize their dreams. Our top-tier benefits and great retirement packages can help you build a rewarding career and lasting future with the State of Illinois. Position Overview Would you like to work for a professional organization which provides steady hours and an exceptional benefits package? How about a workplace with career and personal growth opportunities? The Illinois Department of Revenue is seeking to hire a Legislative Assistant (Administrative Assistant I) to serve as administrative support to the Office of Legislative Affairs located in Springfield, IL. This position is responsible for reviewing and routing highly confidential documents, directing phone calls, and working closely with the Director of Legislative Affairs and staff to ensure the commitments and responsibilities of the Office are met in a timely manner. If you possess strong organizational skills and the ability to prioritize multiple tasks and responsibilities, then we want you! Don’t let this opportunity pass you by. Apply now before time runs out! Essential Functions Under direction, fields constituent and taxpayer inquiries directed to the Illinois Department of Revenue (IDOR) Office of Legislative Affairs (OLA). As Staff Assistant, reviews and assists OLA staff with analysis of pending legislation. Assists with development of IDOR legislative proposals. Serves as administrator of the Legislative Tracking System (LTS). Serves as area timekeeper. Conducts a variety of secretarial and administrative tasks necessary to the operations of the office. Performs other duties as required or assigned, which are reasonably within the scope of the duties enumerated above. Minimum Qualifications Requires knowledge, skill and mental development equivalent to completion of four years of college, preferably with courses in public or business administration. Requires one year of professional experience in a public or private organization, -OR- completion of an agency approved professional management training program. Preferred Qualifications Two (2) years of experience accessing and researching taxpayer accounts in GenTax or similar tax processing software. One (1) year of experience working with legislative processes. Intermediate proficiency with Microsoft Word or similar word processing software. Intermediate proficiency with Microsoft Excel or similar spreadsheet software. Basic proficiency with Microsoft Access or similar database software. Basic proficiency with Adobe Acrobat or similar document manipulating software. One (1) year of experience setting up and conducting meetings and sharing information through Microsoft Teams or similar collaborative digital environment. One (1) year of experience creating and updating presentations in Microsoft PowerPoint or similar presentation software. Conditions of Employment Requires the ability to successfully complete a tax compliance and fingerprint-based background check. Requires the ability to use and secure a state issued mobile device, e.g., cellular phone, laptop computer, tablet, etc. This position has been found to meet the requirements in section 4A-101 of the Illinois Governmental Ethics Act requiring the occupant/employee to file a Statement of Economic Interest. The Illinois Governmental Ethics Act (5 ILCS420/4A et seq.) requires certain state officials and employees to file annual Statements of Economic Interest with the Office of the Secretary of State that will be made available for examination and copying by the public. All employees required to file a Statement of Economic Interest are also required to file the Supplemental Statement of Economic Interest with the Executive Ethics Commission. (See Executive Order 15-09) Fines and penalties apply to untimely filings. The conditions of employment listed here are incorporated and related to any of the job duties as listed in the job description. Agency Statement The Illinois Department of Revenue (IDOR) is responsible for administering the state's tax laws and collecting taxes in a fair, consistent, and efficient manner. Their goal is to provide accurate, timely, and reliable funding and information to both state and local communities. By implementing best practices, IDOR works to continuously improve and enhance accuracy, efficiency, and productivity across all areas of operations and tax administration. In doing so, they aim to earn respect, deliver value, and serve as a trusted source of information for the public. IDOR is a professional governmental entity that prioritizes its employees and actively invests in their success through comprehensive training and engagement. As the proud Platinum recipient of the 2026 Bell Seal for workplace mental health, IDOR cultivates an environment that encourages open dialogue and collaboration on mental health issues. With a strong commitment to diversity—both culturally and professionally—IDOR believes that this inclusive approach leads to a more productive workplace, ultimately benefiting the citizens and taxpayers of Illinois. Economic Interest Reporting: This position has been found to meet the requirements in section 4A-101 of the Illinois Governmental Ethics Act requiring the occupant/employee to file a Statement of Economic Interest. The Illinois Governmental Ethics Act (5 ILCS 420/4A et seq.) requires certain state officials and employees to file annual Statements of Economic Interest with the Office of the Secretary of State that will be made available for examination and copying by the public. All employees required to file a Statement of Economic Interest are also required to file the Supplemental Statement of Economic Interest with the Executive Ethics Commission. (See Executive Order 15-09) Fines and penalties apply to untimely filings. The main form of communication will be through email. Please check your “junk mail”, “spam”, or “other” folder for communication(s) regarding any submitted application(s). You may receive emails from the following addresses: donotreply@SIL-P1.ns2cloud.com systems@SIL-P1.ns2cloud.com

item.title: Election Administrator
item.description: Location: 1 Hamilton County Square - Noblesville, Indiana, 46060 Hamilton County is one of Indiana’s fastest growing, highest educated and wealthiest counties in the state and the Midwest. Two-thirds of the workforce lives and works in the county -- a percent that has remained constant since 2010. Hamilton County is continually recognized in rankings ranging from “Best Cities to Relocate To” and “Best City to Raise a Family” to “Healthiest County in Indiana” and “Happiest Suburbs in the Nation”. Come be a part of all Hamilton County has to offer as we work together to serve the citizens of Hamilton County. Job Description: POSITION DESCRIPTION COUNTY OF HAMILTON, INDIANA POSITION: Election Administrator DEPARTMENT: Elections WORK SCHEDULE: 8:00 a.m. - 4:30 p.m., M-F STATUS: Full-time FLSA STATUS: Non-exempt HOURLY RATE: Up to $51.3741 per hour To perform this position successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed in this document are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Hamilton County provides reasonable accommodation to qualified employees and applicants with known disabilities who require accommodation to complete the application process or perform essential functions of the job, unless the accommodation would cause an undue hardship . Incumbent serves as Election Administrator for the Election Department, responsible for administering election activities according to state and federal regulations, maintaining records, generating reports, and supervising personnel. DUTIES : Supervises and directs department personnel, including assisting with interviewing applicants and hiring, planning/ delegating work assignments, providing orientation, training and corrective instruction, evaluating performance, recommending personnel actions, and maintaining discipline. Answers telephone and assists office visitors, providing assistance and information as requested. Opens and responds to department mail. Generates various reports/lists as needed or as requested, such as population, election statistics, and voter history, addresses and mailing labels. Compiles statistics and mails monthly reports to State Election Commission and Federal Election Commission as required. Attends staff meetings, and other meetings as required or as needed, such as periodic GIS Committee, Election Board, County Council, and/or Board of County Commissioners. Periodically prepares and disseminates press releases regarding elections and voter registration, and occasionally conducts interviews and makes presentations to community groups as requested. Periodically assists Clerk personnel as requested. Periodically sets up petitions as requested. Prepares annual department budget, projecting payroll and other costs, and discussing with Council as requested. Prepares annual budget projections and claims for the election process for city and town officials. Periodically works with ISS Department in upgrading software and hardware as needed. Maintains current knowledge of relevant state guidelines by reading legislative updates and occasionally attending related conferences; makes appropriate changes in local policies and procedures. Election duties : Receives, files and processes declarations of candidacy, including verifying registration, assisting candidates, answering questions as requested, proofreading, filing, entering candidate list on computer, and disseminating to news media and the public. Assists candidates and/or committees in preparing and filing campaign finance reports, including providing information regarding laws and procedures, entering various information on database, mailing deadline and delinquency notices, and compiling and forwarding list of delinquent reports to Election Board. Designs/prepares/enters ballots and enters precinct information on computer semi-annually according to state guidelines, including proofreading to ensure accuracy of all information, printing/preparing ballot fronts for voting machines, and printing sample ballots for each precinct. Maintains inventory of voting machines, entering serial numbers and cost on computer, determining number needed by each precinct, and recording precinct assignment. Oversees absentee voting process, including printing ballots, reviewing applications, verifying eligibility, scheduling and overseeing public test of absentee ballot card voting system. Schedules election and poll workers for precincts for election days, including maintaining log of volunteers, mailing letters requesting volunteers to precinct committee persons, and making new assignments for cancellations. Schedules/provides training for election poll workers regarding election day forms and procedures. Makes changes to poll worker training manual as needed. Arranges/renews contracts with facilities as polling locations, including reviewing state requirements, and arranging building access to deliver voting machines. Prepares and forwards required legal notices to newspapers. Prepares for election days, including determining quantities and ordering forms and supplies, preparing/packing supplies for precinct inspectors according to prescribed list, and unpacking after elections. Provides assistance and information on election day, answering questions and verifying registration of voters. Oversees tallying of votes, including preparing computer system, and assisting canvass board with tallying. Prepares semi-annual certificate of elections and oaths for successful candidates, and documents for Secretary of State, including election certifications, and for federal elections, lists of party chairs, candidates, and delegates to state convention. May periodically update election precinct maps as required for census redistricting, precinct overpopulation, or other statutory requirements, including discussing population growth with city, town and county planners, drawing new lines, writing legal descriptions, and submitting to Indiana Election Commission for approval. Periodically makes speaking presentations to schools and civic groups regarding the election process. Performs related duties as assigned. I. JOB REQUIREMENTS AND DIFFICULTY OF WORK: High school diploma or GED and a minimum of three years of clerical experience, or equivalent combination of education and experience. Thorough knowledge of and ability to research, read, interpret, and apply relevant federal and Indiana voter registration and election codes and procedural manuals. Working knowledge of standard office policies and practices, and ability to apply such knowledge to a variety of interrelated tasks. Ability to supervise and direct department personnel, including assisting with interviewing applicants and hiring, planning/delegating work assignments, providing orientation, training and corrective instruction, evaluating performance, recommending personnel actions, and maintaining discipline. Ability to type with speed and accuracy, and use various department software and office equipment in maintaining accurate records and preparing detailed reports, including computer, fax machine, printer, telephone, copier, voting machine, postage meter, cartridge and absentee card readers, time stamp, and time clock. Working knowledge of standard English grammar, spelling and punctuation, make relevant arithmetic calculations, and prepare and administer department budget Ability to effectively communicate orally and in writing with co-workers, other County departments, other registration sites, poll workers, precinct/party officials, election candidates, related state and local agencies/organizations, and the public, including being sensitive to professional ethics, gender, cultural diversities and disabilities. Ability to effectively coordinate workers and activities at precinct locations during elections. Ability to read, interpret and occasionally manually update county precinct maps. Ability to work on several tasks at the same time, often under time pressure, and complete assignments effectively amidst frequent distractions and interruptions. Ability to understand, memorize, retain, and carry out written or oral instructions and present findings in oral or written form. Ability to competently serve the public with diplomacy and respect, including occasional encounters with irate/hostile persons. Ability to comply with all employer/department personnel policies and work rules, including, but not limited to, attendance, safety, drug-free workplace, and personal conduct. Ability to work alone with minimum supervision, and with others in a team environment. Ability to provide public access to or maintain confidentiality of department information/records according to state requirements. Ability to work extended, weekend and/or evening hours during election periods, and occasionally travel out of town for conferences/meetings, sometimes overnight. II. RESPONSIBILITY: Incumbent performs widely varied, moderately complex duties according to department policies and procedures and state and federal guidelines. Incumbent develops own work objectives, and receives only administrative/advisory direction from supervisor. Errors in incumbent's work are usually prevented through legally defined procedures and are detected through proofreading and/or notification from other departments, agencies or the public. Most undetected errors could result in loss of time for correction and/or inconvenience to voters. Ballot errors could adversely affect election results, could require court resolution, additional cost to County for special elections, and/ or substantial inconvenience to candidates and voters. III. PERSONAL WORK RELATIONSHIPS: Incumbent maintains frequent contact with co-workers, other County departments, other registration sites, poll workers, precinct/party officials, election candidates, related state and local agencies/ organizations, and the public for purposes of ex

item.title: Director Of Policy Advocacy And Government Affairs Feeding Illinois
item.description: Description Reports to: Senior Director of Community Advocacy and Government Affairs [Greater Chicago Food Depository], with a dotted-line reporting relationship to the Executive Director of Feeding Illinois Location: Illinois (Remote; Springfield presence during legislative session, and occasional travel to food banks statewide and Washington D.C.) General Description: The Director of Policy, Government Affairs & Advocacy leads Feeding Illinois’s legislative, regulatory, and public policy strategy at the state and federal levels. This role serves as the chief lobbyist and policy strategist, advancing a proactive agenda that strengthens anti-hunger programs, protects critical nutrition program funding, and promotes equitable policies that address food insecurity across Illinois. The Director builds and maintains strong relationships with lawmakers, state agencies, coalition partners, and community stakeholders, and works closely with member food banks to align advocacy priorities and mobilize collective action. This hire will be paid by the Greater Chicago Food Depository but will be a remote staff person of Feeding Illinois, providing support to any food bank interested in delegating on or collaborating around responsibilities aligned with the duties below. Cover letter submission required for application consideration. About Feeding Illinois Feeding Illinois is the Partner State Association of Feeding America food banks that serve Illinois. Together, they provide food and other services to every county in Illinois through a vast network of member agencies and specialized feeding programs. The number of residents who are hungry in Illinois is staggering and saddening - yet solvable. But only together, with collective support across public and private sectors. As the state association for food banks serving Illinois we work with our members to strengthen and support their efforts to eliminate hunger. Each food bank has identified the specific needs of their communities and has developed a comprehensive array of programs and services to combat hunger in their region. Key Responsibilities and Essential Functions: Government Relations & Lobbying Develop and execute a comprehensive government affairs strategy aligned with organizational and network member priorities. Serve as the primary liaison to state legislators, legislative staff, and relevant state agencies for Feeding Illinois. Monitor, analyze, and influence legislation, budget proposals, and regulatory actions impacting hunger relief and public benefits programs (e.g., SNAP, WIC, The Emergency Food Assistance Program, senior and child nutrition programs, and more). Help plan and execute food bank special events, such as legislator breakfasts, press conferences, service events with elected officials, and more. Policy Development & Analysis Conduct policy research and draft legislative proposals, position papers, testimony, and budget recommendations. Coalition Building & Stakeholder Engagement Enhance the impact and reach of statewide coalitions focused on hunger, poverty, and related social policy issues, such as the Save Our SNAP statewide advocacy coalition Support the engagement of any partner food banks and their pantry networks who opt- in around SNAP advocacy at the Federal and State level Build relationships with advocacy organizations, state associations, community-based groups, and bipartisan stakeholders that drive partnerships with food banks and enhance our collective anti-hunger work. Engage member food banks in coordinated advocacy campaigns and grassroots mobilization efforts. Provide technical assistance and capacity to food banks who want to start or expand efforts to engage their pantries and the neighbors they serve in advocacy through actions such as email listservs, action alerts and their own lobby days. Advocacy Communications Develop advocacy messaging, action alerts, fact sheets, toolkits, and public education materials in support of policy priorities. Provide staffing, volunteer coordination, and project management support to Feeding Illinois food banks who want to engage in non-partisan voter registration/education for elections, and/or special projects like for the U.S. Census. Support partner food banks to communicate about benefit program changes (e.g. SNAP, Medicaid, WIC, Summer EBT, school/summer meals, and more) with their partner networks, such as through newsletters, briefings and/or distribution of resources (i.e. flyers, posters). Leadership & Strategy Manage advocacy, policy, research, communications or other consultants and external partners as needed. Gather and visualize data on the impact of Feeding Illinois food banks (food distributed, households served, purchasing power, etc.) and how they have been impacted by H.R. 1 cuts to SNAP overtime. Lead the monthly Feeding Illinois policy call as a strategy for food banks to align on priority policy, advocacy and government affairs initiatives, and elevate recent touch-points with statewide elected official targets. Qualifications Qualifications : Bachelor’s degree recommended; Master’s Degree or graduate level work in public policy, social work, public health, urban planning, or a related field is preferred. Minimum of 7-10 years of work experience with at least 3 years of experience in lobbying, advocacy, public policy, community organizing, political campaign, or similar experience. Strong knowledge of the advocacy and political landscape in Chicagoland, including trusted relationships at the federal, state and local levels, and a track-record of collaboration with other civic, advocacy, or community organizing groups or coalitions. Proficiency in MS Office-Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and any client relationship management (CRM) database. Exposure: Benefits: • Health, dental, and vision insurance coverage • Employer-paid life and disability insurance • Employee Assistance Program • 403(b) retirement plan with employer contribution • Generous paid time off • Parental leave • On-site gym • $3,000 annual employer-paid ThrivePass lifestyle and wellness benefit program • $250 employee referral bonus

item.title: State Government Affairs Manager Illinois
item.description: About Base Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time. About the Role As Base’s on-the-ground representative in Illinois, you will be the tactical architect of our legislative strategy in the State. You will serve as a high-impact advocate who can navigate the Illinois General Assembly and build relationships with legislators and their staff. You will bridge the gap between our innovative energy technology and state lawmakers, ensuring that legislation shapes a future grid that welcomes our tech and retail electricity solutions. This will be a hybrid role between Austin and Chicago. At Base, our culture is the heartbeat of our success. We are a tight-knit team that thrives on the energy, spontaneous collaboration, and shared purpose that comes from working side-by-side in Austin. For this role, however, we recognize the unique need to be in Illinois. We will therefore look for a candidate who is committed to having a strong presence both in Austin and in Chicago. If based in Chicago, we will ask you to spend your first four to six weeks in Austin and then approximately one week per month thereafter. What You’ll Do Act as the company's advocate at the Illinois State Capitol, building and maintaining relationships with legislators, committee staff, and legislative leadership. Monitor, analyze, and advocate for legislation that impacts our business, tracking bills from introduction through committee and floor action. Draft testimony and written comments for legislative committee hearings that protect our market access and promote tech-forward energy policy. Deploy data-driven arguments to persuade legislators to adopt flexible, technology-friendly standards. Distill legislative shifts into actionable business intelligence for executive leadership. Identify and partner with trade associations, NGOs, and industry peers to amplify our legislative voice and build coalitions around priority bills. Work with the broader policy team to align Illinois legislative strategy with our national policy priorities. What You'll Bring Significant experience in state government affairs, with a heavy emphasis on the Illinois market; experience in energy regulatory affairs is a plus. Proven success lobbying and negotiating with members of the Illinois General Assembly and strong familiarity with how bills move through the statehouse. Ability to translate technical energy and grid concepts into clear, actionable terms for non-technical legislators and staff. A strong presence and exceptional public-speaking skills. Ability to run independently to further a surging business. Comfort with challenging the status quo and preconceived notions of what is possible. Excellent communication skills, with the ability to distill complex concepts into clear, actionable advice. An entrepreneurial mindset that thrives in ambiguity, moves fast, and prioritizes impact. Passion for our work and a commitment to fueling American innovation, security, and prosperity through a more reliable grid for all. About the Team Base's legal, regulatory, and policy team supports the company's ability to build, sell, and operate across the country, covering corporate and commercial legal work, utility regulatory strategy, and state and federal government affairs. Within that team, government affairs focuses on the legislature: shaping and passing the laws that allow a battery company to participate in the market, interconnect with the grid, and get projects permitted. That work happens state by state, through drafting bills, briefing lawmakers, and building coalitions, with the goal of making regulatory approval and local permitting more predictable once the underlying law is in place. The legislation this team pursues often shapes whether and how quickly Base can enter and scale in a given market. Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive. Our Values First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules. Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing. Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset. Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results. Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information. Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in. Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things. Do the best work of your life at Base.

item.title: Material Handler I Order Selection
item.description: Performs distribution center material handling duties that support functions such as; Inbound, Outbound, Returns, Ocomm, City Counter, and Acquisitions operations within the distribution center. Responsible for processing and moving merchandise while maintaining inventory accuracy, productivity, quality, and safety standards. ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS Receive, unload, inspect, sort, stock, pick, pack, stage, and ship merchandise accurately and efficiently. Match item numbers, quantities, manifests, freight bills, and shipping documentation with physical merchandise. Process inbound shipments, outbound orders, store returns, warranty merchandise, acquisitions inventory, and vendor return according to O’Reilly policy. Operate RF scanners, handheld devices, voice-picking systems, warehouse management systems (WMS), and other warehouse technology as required. Properly store and retrieve merchandise from floor locations, shelving, racking systems, and reserve storage areas. Load and unload trailers, containers, route trucks, and freight shipments while ensuring merchandise is secured and protected from damage. Maintain inventory accuracy through proper scanning, labeling, auditing, staging, and discrepancy resolution procedures. Rebox, relabel, sort, and prepare merchandise for shipment or inventory placement as needed. Process warranty merchandise, batteries, recalls, non-stock items, unsaleable merchandise, and vendor return goods according to O’Reilly policy. Follow established procedures for hazardous material handling and disposal in accordance with O’Reilly safety standards and regulatory requirements. Maintain productivity and accuracy standards while completing assigned warehouse tasks and operational workflows. Keep work areas organized, clean, and free of safety hazards. Identify unsafe conditions or practices and report concerns to leadership promptly. Maintain compliance with O’Reilly policies, operational procedures, and quality standards. Perform all other duties as assigned. SKILLS/EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE Required: Ability to accurately match numerical and alphabetical information. Follows established operational, safety, and quality procedures. Maintain safe work environment, including but not limited to safely lifting, moving, and handling merchandise. Willingness to learn warehouse systems, RF technology, and operational processes. Desired: Experience working in a fast-paced warehouse environment. Prior experience handling automotive parts or related merchandise. Experience operating warehouse management systems (WMS), RF scanners, or voice-picking equipment. Experience working within productivity, quality, or performance-driven environments. Proficiency in one or more additional languages. O’Reilly Auto Parts has a proven track record of growth and stability. O’Reilly is full of successful career stories and believes in a strong promote-from-within philosophy, encouraging you to grow your career along with the organization. Total Compensation Package: Competitive Wages & Paid Time Off Stock Purchase Plan & 401k with Employer Contributions Starting Day One Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance with Optional Flexible Spending Account (FSA) Team Member Health/Wellbeing Programs Tuition Educational Assistance Programs Opportunities for Career Growth O’Reilly Auto Parts is an equal opportunity employer. The Company does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin or ancestry (including immigration status or citizenship), sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, pregnancy (including childbirth, lactation, and related medical conditions,) age (40 and over), veteran status, uniformed service member status, physical or mental disability, genetic information (including testing or characteristics) or another protected status as defined by local, state, or federal law, as applicable. Qualified individuals with a disability may be entitled to reasonable accommodation under the Americans with Disabilities Act. If you require a reasonable accommodation during the application or employment process, please send an email to: rar@oreillyauto.com or call (800) 471-7431 option , and provide your requested accommodation, and position details.

item.title: Political Reporter Editor
item.description: If you love to follow politics and tell the stories of election campaigns, parties, and voters, we might be looking for you. Iowa Public Radio is hiring a political reporter-editor in our Des Moines newsroom. You’ll report on state politics for our broadcast and digital platforms and lead our coverage of the Iowa caucuses. In 2028, Iowa will once again kick off the Republican presidential nominating process. You’ll also work with IPR news managers to coordinate our election coverage strategy, guide other IPR reporters in their work on political stories, and help plan our election night coverage. This position is based in Des Moines, Iowa’s largest city and part of the fastest-growing metro area in the Midwest. There are lots of places to catch a concert, enjoy a great meal, watch a game, or bike for miles on one of the area’s many trails. Our ideal candidate is curious, motivated, and has a deep interest in the issues that affect people throughout Iowa. We’re looking for someone with strong editorial judgment and the ability to write quickly and clearly, while telling a good story. If you’re passionate about impactful journalism, care about ethics and diversity, can handle several things at once and are committed to making great radio, we’d love to hear from you. We know there are great candidates who might not exactly fit into what we’ve described here or who have important skills we haven’t listed. If that sounds like you, don’t hesitate to apply and tell us about yourself. Iowa Public Radio is a well-respected and thriving non-profit organization. We offer an excellent benefits package, including health benefits, a retirement plan with a 2-to-1 employer match, immediate accrual of vacation (16 hours monthly) and sick (12 hours monthly) time and a flexible work environment. ANTICIPATED HIRING RANGE : $56,000 - $71,000 SUMMARY : The Political Reporter & Editor serves as Iowa Public Radio’s lead political reporter, covering races for major statewide and federal offices, including the presidential caucus cycle. This person will help coordinate IPR’s wider coverage of political campaigns and races, and assist in editing IPR reporters’ political reporting. This position will also be responsible for coordination and production of special political projects ranging from stories to podcasts. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: Five years of experience working in a professional journalism environment An understanding of local, state and federal political systems Experience working in multimedia platforms, including photographs, video and web platforms Experience operating a variety of broadcast equipment including audio boards, digital editing systems (e.g. Adobe Audition), field recording units, and other production equipment A valid state-issued driver’s license and reliable transportation. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: Three years of experience in political reporting An eye for diverse voices and sources in stories Strong writing skills and experience editing the work of other reporters Experience as a public radio reporter and/or host Firm foundation in journalism ethics, news gathering, and reporting techniques APPLICATION PROCESS : Apply through the position link on the IPR website . For full consideration, applications must include the following: A detailed resume . A narrative carefully detailing how your experience compares to the job duties and qualifications listed for this position. The narrative should not exceed two pages. Sample(s) of your work: Writing samples that include spot news and a news-oriented feature. Online content you have produced (please send links). Online content can be a web build-out of a radio story or news content that was designed to be web-only. Please do not send stories you have produced with the help of a national network. Demo containing one newscast-length story (spot), and one feature-length report (3:00-5:00) that you have edited and produced. If you have one, we’d love to hear a sample of a two-way you did with a program host, or an interview you’ve conducted for a podcast or other audio production. Please upload the demo to Soundcloud or another hosting site and send IPR links. Names and contact information, including email addresses, for three work references , including at least one supervisory reference Employment at Iowa Public Radio is dependent upon successful completion of a criminal background check including a driving record review and reference check. IPR will accept applications through 5:00 p.m. Friday, September 25, 2026 . OUR VALUES : Integrity : We maintain the highest standards of journalism, providing trustworthy and relevant content with meaningful context. Curiosity : We serve an inquisitive audience by asking questions, seeking knowledge, and exploring new ideas. Belonging : We strive to reflect Iowa’s cultural complexity by offering a supportive, equitable space for individuals and communities to tell the stories unique to their lived experiences. Respect : We create a culture of respect for our audience, sources, and staff. Innovation : We support creativity and embrace new ways of serving our audience. OUR COMMITMENT TO EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY : Iowa Public Radio is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Discrimination because of race, color, religion, national origin or sex is prohibited. If you believe you have been a victim of discrimination, please notify the appropriate local, state or federal agency.

item.description: Job Application JOINT COMMITTEE ON LEGISLATIVE MANAGEMENT ROOM 5100, LEGISLATIVE OFFICE BUILDING Hartford, CT 06106-1591 The policy of the Joint Committee on Legislative Management is to provide equal opportunity to all prospective employees without regard to race, religious creed, color, sex, age, national origin, ancestry, veteran status, sexual orientation, marital status, present or past history of mental disorder, learning disability, physical disability except in cases of bona fide occupational qualification or other protected class status under applicable law. Moreover, the Joint Committee on Legislative Management does not discriminate against any “qualified applicant with a disability” and will make reasonable accommodations that do not impose an undue hardship for individuals who are physically challenged or otherwise disabled as defined by the Americans with Disabilities Act. If you require reasonable accommodation to complete this application or any other aspect of the selection process, please contact the Human Resources Administrator in the Office of Legislative Management at (860) 240-0100 or email HRHelp@cga.ct.gov . General Application Instructions Please complete all information requested on this application. Do not include extraneous or non-responsive information. If a question does not apply to you, please write “N/A” in the space provided. The Joint Committee on Legislative Management may reject any application that is incomplete. If you fail to provide complete information on this application form, or if you provide any false or misleading information here or in any part of the application process, your application will not be considered further. If you are employed by the Joint Committee on Legislative Management, the discovery of omissions, misrepresentations or misleading information in the application process will be grounds for termination of employment. Providing References Please provide three (3) professional references on your application. A professional reference is an individual who has been paid to supervise your work and can attest to your work performance, technical skills, and job competencies. If you do not have any or sufficient professional references, please include non-related professionals, such as educators or other professional associates.

item.title: Assistant Legislative Fiscal Analyst
item.description: Title: Assistant Legislative Fiscal Analyst Hiring Range: $70,000 to $80,000, commensurate with relevant education and experience Agency: Senate Finance & Appropriations Committee Location: General Assembly Building Agency Website: https://sfac.virginia.gov/ Recruitment Type: General Public - G Job Duties The Assistant Legislative Fiscal Analyst researches and analyzes legislation, state agency operations, and public policy initiatives. In this capacity, the analyst manages assigned policy and agency portfolios, examines complex financial and operational information, and translates findings into clear, objective analyses, and recommendations for legislative and public audiences. Working alongside experienced fiscal professionals, the successful candidate will build expertise in legislative budgeting, fiscal forecasting, state government operations, and public policy. The position offers a distinctive opportunity to contribute to consequential decisions impacting citizens throughout the Commonwealth while developing a career in nonpartisan legislative service. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES: • Analyze legislation and estimate fiscal and operational impacts. • Research assigned policy areas, state agency operations, and budget proposals. • Support Senate Finance & Appropriations Subcommittees in evaluating legislation and developing budget recommendations. • Monitor assigned agencies and evaluate budget requests, strategic initiatives, and operational performance. • Develop fiscal forecasts and recommendations using financial, economic, demographic, and statistical data. • Prepare data visualizations, reports, issue briefs, and presentations that translate complex findings for legislative audiences. • Contribute to special studies and related Committee assignments. Minimum Qualifications • Bachelor's degree in public policy, public administration, economics, finance, accounting, business administration, political science, statistics, mathematics, data analytics, or a related analytical field (An equivalent combination of relevant education and experience will be considered) • At least two years of progressively responsible professional experience in budget, financial, or policy analysis; government administration; legislative research; program evaluation; economics; public finance; strategic planning; or data analytics. • Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel, including data analysis and visualization. • Demonstrated ability to research, analyze, and synthesize complex fiscal, legislative, policy, and statistical information and communicate findings clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences. • Ability to manage multiple priorities and consistently produce accurate, high-quality work under short deadlines. CORE COMPETENCIES • Analytical Judgment: Uses data, research, and sound reasoning to develop objective conclusions and recommendations. • Communication: Presents complex information clearly, concisely, and appropriately for the audience. • Attention to Detail: Produces accurate, thorough, and reliable work. • Learning Agility and Adaptability: Quickly learns complex subject matter and responds effectively to changing priorities. • Collaboration: Contributes effectively within a small, high-performing professional team. • Professional Integrity and Nonpartisanship: Exercises sound judgment, discretion, and confidentiality while maintaining strict political neutrality in analyses, recommendations, work products, and professional conduct. Additional Considerations PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: • Master's degree in a relevant field. • Government budgeting, finance, or public policy analysis. • Fiscal forecasting, financial modeling, or economic analysis. • Higher education finance, budgeting, policy, or administration. WORKING CONDITIONS: This position requires an on-site presence in Richmond, Virginia, and professional business attire. Legislative sessions and other peak workload periods may require extended hours and work under short, immovable deadlines. Limited telework may be approved outside scheduled legislative sessions. Special Instructions You will be provided a confirmation of receipt when your application and/or résumé is submitted successfully. Please refer to “Your Application” in your account to check the status of your application for this position. TO APPLY Submit a Letter of Interest, Résumé, and College Transcript as one combined PDF document to sfacjobs@sfac.virginia.gov by 11:59 p.m. on Friday, October 16, 2026. Applicant screening will begin immediately. Selected applicants may be asked to provide three professional references and complete a writing exercise and Microsoft Excel assessment during the selection process. EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER The Virginia Senate Finance & Appropriations Committee is an Equal Opportunity Employer. The Commonwealth of Virginia prohibits discrimination based on race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, political affiliation, genetics, or disability in recruiting, selecting, and hiring its workforce. Persons requiring reasonable accommodation in the application process or information in an alternative format may contact SFAC Office Manager Melissa Mayes ( sfacjobs@sfac.virginia.gov ) Contact Information Name: Melissa Mayes Phone: (804) 698-7480 Email: sfacjobs@sfac.virginia.gov In support of the Commonwealth’s commitment to inclusion, we are encouraging individuals with disabilities to apply through the Commonwealth Alternative Hiring Process. To be considered for this opportunity, applicants will need to provide their AHP Letter (formerly COD) provided by the Department for Aging & Rehabilitative Services (DARS), or the Department for the Blind & Vision Impaired (DBVI). Service-Connected Veterans are encouraged to answer Veteran status questions and submit their disability documentation, if applicable, to DARS/DBVI to get their AHP Letter. Requesting an AHP Letter can be found at AHP Letter or by calling DARS at 800-552-5019. Note : Applicants who received a Certificate of Disability from DARS or DBVI dated between April 1, 2022- February 29, 2024, can still use that COD as applicable documentation for the Alternative Hiring Process.

item.title: Public Policy And Comment Analysis Specialist Hybrid Role Reston Va
item.description: PUBLIC POLICY & COMMENT ANALYSIS SPECIALIST Are you interested in assisting Federal agencies by analyzing public feedback on current and emerging federal policy issues and regulatory programs? Do you want to apply your education and experience to help government agencies improve the way they develop and implement regulations, policies, and programs? Our Regulatory, Policy and Economics (RPE) portfolio has over 30 years of experience supporting the design, implementation, and improvement of federal programs and is seeking an experienced public policy analyst and comment analysis project contributor/manager to join them. Join our multidisciplinary team of regulatory specialists, policy analysts, economists, and attorneys. We combine legal, policy, economic, and scientific research and analysis to solve unique public policy challenges through innovative, accurate, timely, and high-quality products and services. Our dynamic work environment involves working on multiple projects simultaneously and providing a wide range of support services for a variety of federal clients. This full-time position is available immediately and primarily located in Reston, VA (i.e., in the DC Metro area) with flexibility for telework considered. Job Responsibilities: The Public Policy and Comment Analysis Specialist will be focused primarily on the review, processing, and analysis of public comments on highly scrutinized and often controversial public policy topics. The Public Policy and Comment Analysis Specialist will contribute to and assist in directing teams of ICF staff on individual tasks and whole projects associated with comment analysis support for Federal regulatory initiatives. This position will also interact directly with federal agency clients to understand their goals and objectives for each project, confirm and clarify client direction, and to ensure that ICF’s analysis and deliverables meet a high level of quality. Duties also include contributing to federal rulemaking documents, policy papers, and technical background documents, as well as technical writing and editing, report production, and assist in managing discrete tasks and small teams of staff to work toward a milestone or deliverable. The Public Policy and Comment Analysis Specialist will work within and help manage interdisciplinary teams supporting federal government client agencies that develop and implement regulatory programs affecting public health, the environment, energy, homeland security and immigration, labor and workforce issues, transportation, and other national priorities. What you will do: Support federal agency efforts to transparently analyze public comments received on proposed agency rules and initiatives Provide advice to clients relating to the analysis, processing, and management of public feedback received on agency initiatives Participate in short- and long-term engagements to support federal clients whose responsibilities are to develop policies and craft regulations that implement a desired policy, explain the rationale of the rulemaking to interested parties, and implement the regulatory requirements Perform detailed quality control reviews of draft deliverables prior to submittal to clients Assist agencies in drafting, editing, and formatting federal rulemaking documents Provide day-to-day technical direction to project staff Immerse oneself rapidly in varied projects for multiple clients Assist in managing project/task teams and develop and monitor project budgets and schedules Assist in managing day-to-day client relationships, ensuring client satisfaction and working to develop long-term client relationships Drafting reports and presentations Minimum Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree (in Public Policy, Political Science, or a related field). Minimum 3 years of related work experience in a government agency, professional services firm, or related environment; OR Master's degree (in Public Policy or a related field) or equivalent (e.g., JD, MPA) plus a minimum of 2 years of related work experience in a government agency, professional services firm, or related environment . Demonstrated understanding of and experience providing comment analysis support for federal agency rulemakings and initiatives. U.S. Citizenship is required per federal contracts. Ability to obtain and maintain a moderate-level government security clearance. Professional skills we are looking for: 1+ years of experience working on comment analysis projects related to federal regulatory programs and issues. Strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational, time management, and decision-making skills. Ability to prioritize and work on multiple projects under strict deadlines in a fast-paced environment. Excellent written and oral communications skills. Strong attention to detail and collaborative approach. Proficiency in MS Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint). Experience providing day to day oversight of individuals or teams. #Indeed #LI-CC1 #RPEJBS Bot and Third-Party Applications Please note that this application must be submitted directly by the applicant for consideration. Failure to do so may result in the application being excluded for consideration . item.title: Congressional Liaison Officer N2701
item.description: Position is 100% Onsite Who We Are : Founded in 2007, SimIS Inc. is an innovative information technology solution Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) that models future environments, requirements, and capabilities, and then secures the enterprise from internal and external threats compliant with Federal, State, and industry standard governance to ensure client mission success. Our performance standard is “excellence,” with an outcomes-based, quality focus in our services and products, guided by our core values of honesty (in word and deed), relationships (confidence and trust with clients and partners), teamwork (shared goals, mission, and purpose), loyalty (allegiance to our client and team), and importance of others (work and win as a team). SimIS is currently recruiting for the listed position and is contingent upon award. The position is anticipated to be “on site.” Job Description: SimIS, Inc. is seeking provides support for the role of Liaison Officer to the U.S. Congress to serve as our customers forward presence in Washington, D.C., representing interests, monitoring legislative dynamics, and cultivating strong relationships with Members of Congress, staffers, and relevant committees. SimIS, Inc. seeks a Congressional Liaison Officer to ensure our customers visibility on Capitol Hill, strengthening their network within the U.S. legislative branch, and supporting efforts to anticipate and adapt to U.S. defense priorities. Qualifications: Master's degree in Political Science, International Relations, Economics, Law, or a similar field. BS degree with significant Congressional staff experience will be considered. Five years of experience working with or within the U.S. Congress, particularly on defense, appropriations, and foreign policy issues. In-depth knowledge of the U.S. Congressional process, including authorization and appropriations cycles. A proven track record of success in a government relations position, with a demonstrated ability to manage a legislative portfolio, understand and communicate complex policies, and successfully navigate the legislative process. Excellent communication skills, particularly the ability to interface effectively with elected officials, policymakers, and key Congressional and federal staff, verbally, in writing, and through professional interpersonal skills, to inform, educate, and persuade in support of defense initiatives. Ability to work and communicate with colleagues across departments to gather the resources, skills, and expertise necessary to convey the customers message on Capitol Hill and across administrations. Ability to represent and advocate the organization's policy positions to Congress, the Executive Branch, think tanks, and other relevant stakeholders. Ability to develop and implement long- and short-term action plans that lead to the accomplishment of initiatives on innovation, capability development, and other assigned topics. Responsibilities: Monitor and analyze the U.S. defense budget process, from planning to execution, highlighting implications for NATO. Track ongoing Congressional defense reforms and assess their impact on NATO transformation. Provide strategic reporting on Congressional debates and decisions concerning Ukraine and broader Euro-Atlantic security. Assess budget issues linked to the U.S. troop presence in Europe, with specific attention to burden-sharing debates. Analyse the political dynamics of defense-related legislation, identifying key influencers and agendas. Plan and conduct informal engagements, including dinners and meetings, with legislators and staffers to promote ACT visibility. Monitor legislative initiatives, hearings, and committee activities relevant to NATO. Manage relationships with Members of Congress and provide tailored briefings on ACT and NATO priorities. Coordinate with U.S. executive agencies, NATO missions, and Allied embassies to ensure message coherence. Produce regular reports for SACT and POLAD on Congressional trends, risks, and opportunities.. Benefits: Medical, Dental, and Vision Short-Term Disability (at no cost to you) & Long-Term Disability Life Insurance 401(k) Savings Plan Flex Spending Accounts Tuition Assistance Program Professional Development Paid Time Off (PTO) 11 Federal Holidays each year SimIS, Inc. is an EOE / M / F / Disability / VET / Drug Free Employer

item.title: Legislative Land Use Planner
item.description: $88,153.20 - $154,268 USD yearly Loudoun County Government has been named one of Forbes' 2025 Best Large Employers! We’re proud to be recognized nationally for our commitment to employee satisfaction and excellence in public service. At Loudoun County, we bring together talented professionals from all backgrounds to make a meaningful impact in a dynamic, growing community — that’s The Loudoun Difference . Welcome and thank you for your interest in employment with Loudoun County Government! ALL SECTIONS OF THE APPLICATION MUST BE COMPLETED IN ITS ENTIRETY. THE RESUME IS CONSIDERED SUPPLEMENTAL INFORMATION ONLY. APPLICATIONS THAT ARE INCOMPLETE OR INDICATE 'SEE RESUME' WILL NOT BE TAKEN INTO CONSIDERATION. _________________________________________________________________________________________ Introduction Do you enjoy leading teams and collaborating with stakeholders to shape land use policies? If you thrive in fast-paced environments solving land use issues, consider joining Loudoun County, Virginia’s Department of Planning and Zoning as a Legislative Land Use Planner. You’ll manage the review process for legislative land development applications in a growing community near Washington, D.C. After an initial training period, you may telework two days per week. Job Summary The Department is committed to delivering high-quality customer service and presents unique opportunities for professionals to advance their careers in the planning field. Employees benefit from exposure to a wide range of experiences, including working on projects in rural, historic, suburban, and urban parts of Loudoun County. These opportunities include involvement in innovative initiatives such as data center development, multi-unit residential complexes, and commercial spaces, allowing staff to broaden their expertise in diverse planning environments. The Department is seeking an experienced professional to play a significant role in implementing the Loudoun 2019 Comprehensive Plan and contribute as part of the team guiding future development in the county. In this role, you will serve as a project manager overseeing a caseload of medium-to-large-scale land development applications. Specific responsibilities include: • Analyzing proposed development projects for compliance with county policies and ordinances. • Coordinating the review process with other departments and external agencies. • Providing clear, actionable recommendations to the Planning Commission and Board of Supervisors at regular night meetings. You will also address land use issues related to projects such as data center development, energy infrastructure, multi-unit residential communities, and commercial uses, contributing to the high quality of life in Loudoun County. The ideal candidate will have advanced expertise in zoning laws, environmental regulations, and urban design principles, along with at least five years of experience successfully managing land development projects. Strong presentation skills are essential, as is the ability to deliver clear, cohesive technical analyses to decision-makers, meet deadlines, and effectively manage multiple assignments. Candidates with a proven track record of leading large-scale urban development initiatives and collaborating with diverse stakeholders will be preferred, demonstrating a high level of professionalism and specialized knowledge in land use planning. This position is eligible for a $6,000 hiring bonus in accordance with the County’s Hiring and Retention Bonus Program. Salary commensurate with experience. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Planning, Public Administration, Public Policy, Business Administration, or a related field; five (5) years of related work experience; or equivalent combination of education and experience. Progressively responsible work experience at a level that required management of complex planning and land use projects is preferred. Preferred Qualifications Include: • American Institute of Certified Planners (AICP) certification • Certified Zoning Administrator (CZA) • Certified Zoning Official (CZO) • Project Management Professional (PMP) • Experience with ArcGIS, Bluebeam Revu software, and/or EnerGov software Job Contingencies and Special Requirements Attendance and presentation at regular night meetings after normal business hours is required, to discuss project approvals and gather feedback from community stakeholders. Candidates are required to successfully complete both criminal and driving background checks. This position calls for an analytical thinker with real-world experience in land planning, such as developing zoning plans, reviewing site designs for compliance with local regulations, or overseeing resource preservation initiatives. Typical responsibilities include evaluating building and conceptual site development plans/plats, preparing reports for the Planning Commission and the Board of Supervisors, and coordinating with multiple departments to ensure projects align with community standards. The ability to efficiently manage a high case load, prioritize tasks, analyze policies and regulations, and meet critical deadlines is essential. Strong written and verbal communication skills are required, along with the flexibility to adapt to a range of situations involving staff, applicants, governmental officials, and citizens. In addition to the daily responsibilities, this role provides opportunities for professional development and career advancement through ongoing training, exposure to complex projects, and regular interaction with top governmental officials. _________________________________________________________________________________________ Equal Employment Opportunity Loudoun County Government prides itself on fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace that promotes employee wellness and work-life balance. As an equal opportunity employer, we consider all qualified applicants regardless of age, color, disability, gender identity, genetic information, national origin, political affiliation, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation or other non-merit factors. Reasonable Accommodation Applicants who wish to request a reasonable accommodation during the recruitment process should call Human Resources directly at 703-777-0213 or email Human Resources.
