item.title: Project Manager Rfp And Vendor Selection
item.description: Role: Project Manager RPF and Vendor Selection Location: 3 days onsite in PA PS: Onsite Interview for the role would be conducted in Harrisburg PA, no websam / online interviews The position will fulfill the roles of Project Manager of the Request for Proposal (RFP) development and vendor selection. It will support the Commissions in all facets of the Commonwealth's RFP requirements in development, submission, evaluation, negotiation, and award of contract. The position will maintain the role of advocate for the Commissions at every stage of the RFP procurement process. The successful candidate for this position must possess direct project management experience of similar sized scope and complexity of projects that include a software development life cycle, order fulfillment and customer/sales agent support. Familiarity with natural resource management, conservation, and outdoor recreation is highly desired. Technical writing skills are preferred. The successful applicant must be capable of working independently to meet the objective of developing an RFP using the Commonwealth's format and assuring compliance with IT policies, procedures, and procurement rules. The RFP must succinctly capture both Commissions' licensing and other identified program requirements. The project manager is responsible for maintaining project documents, developing/monitoring the project schedule, capturing meeting notes and document/tracking action items throughout the life of the project. The project manager will also develop the Commissions' RFP document and manage the submission and assist with the vendor evaluation and final contract negotiations Project Management: Use an approved project management methodology to develop, control, and maintain a project management plan and schedule that will encompass all facets of writing a comprehensive RFP, vendor bid management, evaluation of submissions, negotiation, and contract award. RFP Development and Submission: Utilize Commonwealth management directives, Department of General Services procurement rules, and Governor's Office of Administration/Office of Information Technology policies and procedures to develop an RFP for the Commissions' approval and submission that will document the requirements for a licensing system that will replace all existing system functionality as well as documents all requested and approved enhancements. Develop and document the Commissions' program requirements to meet business specifications. Conduct regularly scheduled meetings with subject matter experts, key stakeholders, and Commissions' Offices of Chief Counsel to ensure expected outcomes are met. Research, document, and recommend best management practices from other states for automated licensing systems that should be considered as enhancements. Document security requirements in accordance with Commissions' and Commonwealth policies, as well as industry standards and best practices, especially as it refers to system and data security. Preparation of SLAs: Prepare Service Level Agreements (SLAs) for inclusion in the subsequent RFP. This includes license requirements, SLAs, security requirements, and contractual instruments. An SLA is a part of a service contract where the level of service is formally defined. The Commissions requires the vendor to have experience in developing RFPs and SLAs for turn-key point-of-sale business processes and to work closely with the Commissions' Offices of Chief Counsel in developing all SLAs. RFP Evaluation Assistance: Develop and maintain vendor response evaluation metrics for the scoring of all qualified vendors. Assist the Commissions in evaluating proposals submitted through the subsequent RFP process to ensure vendors meet all mandatory RFP requirement as established by the Commonwealth, Department of General Services, and the Governor's Office of Administration/Office of Information Technology. Assist with question/answer compilation and response, vendor demonstrations, proposal evaluation, and contract negotiations. Provide consultation to Commissions on the scoring of vendors. Provide consultation on negotiating with selected vendor and contract award.

item.title: Director Government Affairs
item.description: Position Summary The Director will develop and maintain strong relationships with Members of Congress and congressional staff and advocate for CTA’s policy priorities across a broad range of issues affecting the consumer technology industry. The Director will serve as a key member of CTA’s federal lobbying team, working across the organization’s policy portfolio and helping identify opportunities to advance CTA’s policy priorities on Capitol Hill. The Director will also lead CTA’s federal policy and regulatory work on transportation and mobility, including autonomous vehicles and emerging transportation technologies. Key Responsibilities Primary: Build and maintain relationships with Members of Congress and congressional staff across both the House and Senate and serve as a key democratic relationship lead for CTA on Capitol Hill. Lead or co-lead CTA policy development and member working groups within the transportation portfolio. Lead CTA’s federal policy and regulatory engagement on transportation, mobility, autonomous vehicles, and related emerging technologies. Advocate for CTA’s legislative and policy priorities across the organization’s broader technology agenda. Identify opportunities to advance CTA priorities through legislation, congressional engagement, coalition activity, and political relationship-building. Prepare statements, testimony, talking points, briefing materials, and other advocacy materials for congressional engagement. Draft and submit comments to federal regulatory agencies on transportation and mobility issues. Organize and participate in congressional meetings, lobbying days, political events, policy briefings, technology demonstrations, and CES. Represent CTA before policymakers and at industry meetings, policy events, panels, and, as appropriate, in the press. Work closely with CTAPAC to develop and strengthen relationships with current and emerging technology leaders in Congress. Additional: Monitor congressional activity and identify legislative and political developments affecting CTA and its members. Liaise with industry coalitions and outside stakeholders, particularly on transportation and mobility issues. Support CTA thought leadership through articles, position papers, blogs, and other policy communications. Support CTA engagement on state and local transportation issues as appropriate. Provide member companies with relevant updates on congressional hearings, agency actions, and other policy developments. Support federal lobbying efforts outside the Director’s primary policy portfolio as needed. Perform other duties as required by business needs. Qualifications Work Experience: At least 6–8 years of experience in federal government affairs, congressional affairs, or public policy. Significant experience working in or with the U.S. Congress. Demonstrated experience building and maintaining relationships with Members of Congress and senior congressional staff. Experience with transportation, mobility, autonomous vehicles, or technology policy strongly preferred. Experience researching, analyzing, and communicating legislative and regulatory issues. Skills/Capabilities/Technical: Strong understanding of Congress, the legislative process, and the federal political environment. Excellent political judgment and ability to identify opportunities to advance organizational priorities. Exceptional relationship-building skills and the ability to develop, maintain, and leverage internal and external relationships. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work effectively across multiple policy areas and respond quickly to changing legislative priorities. Education/Trainings: Bachelor’s degree in political science or related field preferred, or commensurate experience. Additional Information: Must have flexibility to attend industry events in the early morning and evenings, and occasional weekends. Some travel required. About CTA Want to work at the forefront of innovation and make an impact across the technology industry? The Consumer Technology Association (CTA)® is the leading voice of the technology industry, representing innovators and shaping the future through advocacy, insights, and global events like CES®. When you join CTA, you become part of a team that values collaboration, transparency, and meaningful impact. At CTA, our culture is built by our people. We are: Staff-Focused – We value every voice and seek input across teams Transparent & Collaborative – We foster open communication and teamwork Open & Honest – We encourage thoughtful feedback, open dialogue, and continuous growth. Impact-Driven – We focus on work that drives meaningful results Adaptable & Forward-Thinking – We embrace innovation and change CTA has been recognized for its strong workplace culture, including honors such as the CARE Award (for 16 consecutive years), Washingtonian Best Places to Work, and the Cigna Healthy Workforce Designation (Gold Level). Compensation & Benefits CTA is committed to transparency and equitable pay practices. The anticipated salary range for this position is $170,000 – $180,000 , with final compensation determined based on experience, skills, and internal equity. This role may be eligible for bonus or additional compensation, where applicable. CTA offers a comprehensive benefits package supporting your health, financial well-being, and work-life balance, including: Health & Wellness – Medical, dental, and vision coverage with telemedicine access, wellness programs, and an on-site fitness center Financial Benefits – 401(k) with 100% employer match up to 6%, student loan assistance, and commuter benefits. Unique to CTA — a mortgage assistance program that may include eligibility for a forgivable home purchase loan of up to $40,000. item.description: Job Description Legislative Affairs Assistant NRECA is a unique national trade association providing advocacy, financial services and business support services to over 900 consumer owned electric cooperatives across the country. NRECA employees are united by our mission, inclusive culture, collaborative workplace and commitment to service excellence. As a “best place to work” employer, we operate with integrity, transparency and a spirit of innovation. As a member of our Government Relations department, you will be joining a team that advocates on behalf of NRECA members on federal legislative and regulatory matters and in national policy forums and develops and trains our grassroots to impact policies at the federal, state and local level. NRECA has the top policy brand reputation among trade associations in Washington, D.C. for the last 4 consecutive years. Summary of Position The person in this role serves as administrative and programmatic support to the NRECA Legislative Affairs team. They will assist in the implementation of advocacy programs, manage the day-to-day meeting and travel schedules of the Vice President, schedule meetings with internal and external parties, draft and proofread correspondence, process expense reimbursements, process invoices, and complete other administrative tasks as required. This position requires 5 full days in office with flexibility offered at the discretion of management. Qualifications Required Qualifications and Skills 2+ years of work or leadership experience with progressive levels of responsibility. 1+ year of experience in government relations or as an administrative assistant working for mid-to-upper level executives. item.title: Legislative Analyst
item.description: Legislative Analyst City of Leander Leander, Texas, United States Full-time 8 days ago $76,169.60 - $91,395.20 USD yearly Summary Works under the supervision of the Assistant City Manager, with moderate latitude for the use of initiative and independent judgement. This position plays a key role in establishing and maintaining relationships with officials from local, state, and federal governments and agencies. Under the direction of the Assistant City Manager, it analyzes legislation that affects the City of Leander and plans strategic legislative activities regarding it. Please note that final offered salary will depend on the education/qualifications of the selected candidate. Essential Duties & Required Qualifications Essential Duties and Responsibilities Develops policies, procedures, guidelines, standards, templates, and tools related to the legislative program. Ensures that legislative program activities are aligned with advocacy initiatives, strategic priorities, and city management directives. Coordinates, compiles, reviews, and synthesizes impact analyses, regulatory and legislative analyses, and other input provided by outside resources. Monitors political news and developments, debates, news conferences and press releases, political campaigns, platforms, statements and other government relations occurrences, as they relate to public policy issues. Responds to and assists with inquiries from City Council members as well as those of City Administration. Assists with the development and implementation of Mayor and City Council program initiatives as needed. Serves as the grants liaison for the City Manager’s Office to departments and external agencies. Responds to the public seeking information or assistance. Coordinates with City departments on a wide variety of issues and develops collaborative relationships with them. Attends evening/weekend meetings, special events, and other activities as needed. Attends City Council meetings, boards/commission and the meetings of other area governing bodies as needed. Participates in various conferences at the regional, state, and national level as needed. Acts as a point of contact for other agencies and will coordinate responses to requests. Attends sessions of the Texas Legislature in order to engage with legislators and their staff regarding legislation that would impact the City of Leander. Tracks and summarizes important legislation, hearings, and committee activities. Performs other duties as assigned. Required Education and Experience Bachelor's degree or higher from an accredited four-year college or university in Public or Business Administration, Political Science, Public Policy, or a related field. Four years or more of experience managing legislative projects and initiatives for a local, state, or federal entity. Required Certificates and Licenses Valid Texas Class C Driver's License or equivalent from any U.S. State. Preferred Qualifications Experience working directly with City Administration and local, state, and federal elected officials. Master’s degree or higher from an accredited four-year college or university in Public or Business Administration, Political Science, Public Policy, or a related field. Experience working with the Texas State Legislature in a similar role. Knowledge, Skills & Abilities Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Considerable knowledge of legislative analysis. Considerable knowledge of the Texas Legislature and the legislative process. Considerable knowledge or administrative methods and practices. Knowledge of local government operations, policies, and procedures. Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to build positive working relationships with Council members, staff, and the public. Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment. Ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise discretion when dealing with sensitive information. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex information clearly and concisely Ability to work with frequent interruptions and changes in priorities. Ability to communicate with other employees and the public in a courteous and diplomatic manner. Skill in handling multiple tasks and prioritizing. Analyze situations and adopt quick, effect, and reasonable courses of action. Skill in using computers and related software applications, including MS Office Excel and PowerPoint. Skill in data analysis and problem solving. Ability to plan strategically. Ability to develop and maintain effective working relationships with City employees, the public, elected officials, and boards and commissions. Ability to build and maintain relationships with government officials, stakeholders, and community members. Physical Demands & Additional Information Physical Demands While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand, walk, sit, use hands to handle items, talk, and hear. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, and ability to adjust focus. The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be considered to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by individuals assigned to this job. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required of personnel so classified in this position. Job offer and continuation of employment with the City of Leander is contingent upon: Proof of education, certification(s) and experience as listed on the employment application based on the job posting requirements. Satisfactory results from a pre-employment criminal history background and driving record check. Legal authorization to work in the United States without sponsorship. * Compliance with the Selective Service Registration for male US citizens and immigrants, who are ages 18-25. *The City of Leander participates in E-Verify! Information from each new employee’s Form I-9 will be provided to the Social Security Administration (SSA) and, if necessary, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to confirm work authorization. The City of Leander is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity, and sexual orientation), national origin, age (40 or older), disability or genetic information in employment. Applicants should communicate requests for disability-related accommodations during the application process to our Human Resources Department at hr@leandertx.gov or 512-528-2708. item.title: Director State Legislative Regulatory Affairs
item.description: Since opening our first self-storage facility in 1972, Public Storage has grown to become the largest owner and operator of self-storage facilities in the world. With thousands of locations across the U.S. and Europe, and more than 170 million net rentable square feet of real estate, we're also one of the largest landlords. We've been recognized as A Great Place to Work by the Great Place to Work Institute. And, our employees have also voted us as having Best Career Growth , ranked us in the Top 5% for Work Culture , and in the Top 10% for Diversity and Inclusion . We're a member of the S&P 500 and FT Global 500 . Our common and preferred stocks trade on the New York Stock Exchange. Public Storage is the nation’s leading self-storage provider, recognized for its iconic orange doors and commitment to delivering simple, reliable solutions to millions of customers across the country. We are expanding our creative team to enhance our consistent and engaging visual brand presence. The Director, State Legislative & Regulatory Affairs will monitor, assess, and help shape state and local policy developments affecting Public Storage and the self-storage industry. This role will serve as a strategic advisor to Legal, Compliance, Operations, Revenue Management, Marketing, Risk, and senior leadership on legislative and regulatory issues, with particular emphasis on consumer protection, pricing, advertising and marketing, lien laws, insurance, property operations, taxation, privacy, and other matters affecting a nationwide consumer-facing real estate business. The successful candidate will bring deep experience monitoring and managing legislative and regulatory activity across multiple states, translating complex developments into practical business guidance, and leading coordinated efforts among internal stakeholders, outside counsel, consultants, contract lobbyists, trade associations, and cross-functional teams nationwide. A law degree is not required; Public Storage is seeking a seasoned public policy, state government affairs, or regulatory affairs leader who can build scalable processes and manage a national portfolio of issues with sound judgment and executive presence. Key Responsibilities Monitor, analyze, and report on state and local legislative and regulatory developments affecting Public Storage, including proposed legislation, administrative rulemaking, attorney general activity, agency guidance, and emerging policy trends. Develop and manage a nationwide issue-tracking process that identifies risks and opportunities across multiple states and escalates priority matters to Legal, Compliance, Operations, and senior business leaders. Lead the coordination of state advocacy strategies, including developing policy positions, drafting testimony and comment letters, recommending legislative language, and supporting direct engagement with policymakers and regulators. Manage and coordinate external resources, including contract lobbyists, outside counsel, consultants, trade associations, and coalition partners, to ensure consistent strategy, timely intelligence, and effective execution across jurisdictions. Partner with internal stakeholders to assess the operational, financial, compliance, customer, and reputational impact of proposed laws and regulations and recommend practical response strategies. Translate complex legislative and regulatory developments into clear, actionable guidance for executives and business teams. Support regulatory and legislative strategies related to consumer protection, pricing, advertising and marketing, lien laws, insurance and risk, property operations, tax, privacy, call center practices, and other issues affecting the self-storage industry. Build and maintain relationships with state legislators, regulators, agency staff, attorneys general offices, governors’ offices, trade associations, business coalitions, and other external stakeholders. Prepare briefings, memoranda, issue summaries, talking points, testimony, correspondence, and executive-level reports on key legislative and regulatory matters. Track lobbying, political, gift, ethics, and disclosure obligations in partnership with Legal and Compliance to support adherence to applicable federal, state, and local requirements. Support integration and compliance planning for business expansion, acquisitions, entry into new jurisdictions, and changes in state operating requirements. Manage cross-functional workstreams and nationwide teams to ensure alignment, accountability, and timely execution on priority legislative and regulatory matters. 10–12+ years of relevant experience in state government affairs, legislative affairs, regulatory affairs, public policy, trade association advocacy, or a related role. Demonstrated experience monitoring, analyzing, and managing legislative and regulatory developments across multiple states. Proven ability to manage nationwide teams, external consultants, contract lobbyists, and cross-functional stakeholders in a matrixed environment. Strong understanding of state legislative and regulatory processes, including bill tracking, committee activity, rulemaking, public comment processes, coalition advocacy, and policymaker engagement. Experience developing advocacy strategies and translating policy developments into business, operational, and compliance recommendations. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to draft testimony, comment letters, policy briefs, executive summaries, and strategic recommendations. Strong project management skills, with the ability to prioritize competing issues, manage deadlines across jurisdictions, and create scalable systems for tracking and reporting. Sound judgment, discretion, and ability to advise senior leaders on sensitive, fast-moving, and high-impact public policy matters. Bachelor’s degree in political science, public policy, public administration, business, communications, or a related field required; advanced degree, public policy degree, or J.D. welcome but not required. Ability to travel regularly to state capitals, industry meetings, company locations, and external stakeholder engagements as needed. Preferred Experience Experience working for or with a national, multi-state, consumer-facing, real estate, retail, property management, financial services, logistics, or regulated services business. Experience managing issue portfolios involving consumer protection, pricing, advertising and marketing, contracts, lien laws, insurance, tax, privacy, or property operations. Familiarity with legislative tracking and government affairs platforms such as Quorum, FiscalNote, LexisNexis State Net, PolicyNote, or similar tools. Experience working with trade associations, coalitions, attorneys general offices, state regulatory agencies, and bipartisan policymaker networks. Experience building a legislative and regulatory affairs function, including processes for issue intake, tracking, escalation, stakeholder engagement, and executive reporting. Key Attributes Strategic, practical, and business-oriented approach to public policy and regulatory risk. Ability to operate independently while keeping internal stakeholders aligned and informed. Executive presence and credibility with senior leaders, policymakers, regulators, and external partners. Comfort managing ambiguity, competing priorities, and fast-moving legislative sessions across multiple jurisdictions. Collaborative style with the ability to lead through influence across legal, operational, compliance, and business teams. Public Storage is an equal opportunity employer and embraces diversity. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or any other protected status. All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply. **Sponsorship for Work Authorization is not available for this posting. Candidates must be authorized to work in the U.S. without restrictions or requiring sponsorship now or in the future. We do not provide training plans or support for F-1 OPT, STEM OPT extensions, or future visa sponsorship.** REF4467F

item.title: Visiting Assistant Professor Of Political Science
item.description: Job Title Visiting Assistant Professor of Political Science Agency Texas A&M University - Corpus Christi Department College Of Liberal Arts Proposed Minimum Salary Commensurate Job Location Corpus Christi, Texas Job Type Faculty Job Description The College of Liberal Arts is seeking a Visiting Assistant Professor of Political Science in American Politics to begin in Fall 2027. The successful candidate will show excellent and enthusiastic teaching skills and demonstrate the ability to work in a team environment. Course assignments will be undergraduate courses across the Political Science curriculum. Teaching assignments may include classroom (face-to-face), hybrid, and online classes with various class sizes. Candidates should be prepared to teach core curriculum requirements such as American government and state and local government (emphasis on Texas). In addition, candidates will contribute to the teaching needs of the Political Science major including courses such as introduction to political science, Mexican American politics, research methods, and the senior capstone. The normal teaching load will be 4-4. The Department of Social Sciences (DSOC) is a multi-disciplinary department in the College of Liberal Arts that offers undergraduate degrees in Political Science and Criminal Justice and the graduate degree of Master of Public Administration. Through its contribution to the core curriculum, Political Science is one of the largest generators of student credit hours for the university. The Criminal Justice program is one of the largest undergraduate majors on campus. The MPA program is the second largest graduate program in the College of Liberal Arts. DSOC faculty are leaders on campus, in the community, and in their disciplines. We value excellence and work daily to support the University’s Islander Impact 2030 Overarching Goal to be nationally recognized for student success, academic achievement, research, creative activity, innovation, and service excellence. Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi is a vibrant, Hispanic and Minority Serving R2 Doctoral Research Institution that proudly provides a solid academic reputation, renowned faculty, and highly rated degree programs since 1947. The University has a heritage of teaching excellence with innovation in research and community engagement as part of the distinguished Texas A&M System. TAMU-CC is the only university in the nation located on its own island, at the heart of the Texas Gulf Coast. With palm tree lined pathways throughout the campus, nearby natural wetlands, a scenic hike-and-bike trail and pristine views of the beach and bays, Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi is a first-choice institution. Required Qualifications: Doctoral degree in Political Science or a closely related discipline from an accredited university. Advanced ABD will be considered; degree must be conferred at the time of appointment. Ability to teach courses in the Political Science program (including American government, state/Texas and local government, introduction to political science, research methods, and senior capstone). Ability to teach in a variety of formats and class sizes to include classroom, hybrid, and online courses. Commitment to excellence in teaching and student mentoring. TO APPLY : https://www.tamucc.edu/human-resources/careers/index.php All required documentation must be submitted to be considered for the position. A completed application will include: A letter of application addressing qualifications listed above including a teaching philosophy and/or evidence of excellence in teaching A curriculum vitae Three professional references including name, address, title, telephone number, and email addresses. Unofficial copies of graduate transcripts Application deadline: Sunday, November 1st, 2026 Position start date: Fall 2027 For questions about the position, please contact Dr. Isla Schuchs Carr, Department Chair, at isla.schuchscarr@tamucc.edu . NOTE: Employment may be impacted by the Presidential proclamation issued on September 19, 2025 and the moratorium issued by Texas Governor Abbott on January 27, 2026. All positions are security-sensitive. Applicants are subject to a criminal history investigation, and employment is contingent upon the institution’s verification of credentials and/or other information required by the institution’s procedures, including the completion of the criminal history check. item.title: Regulatory Affairs And Public Policy Senior Associate
item.description: At Rowan Digital Infrastructure, we are transforming data center delivery for speed and scale. Our mission is to deliver best-in-class data center solutions to hyperscale customers who share our commitment to sustainability, and to do so with an unwavering focus on efficiency, quality, and flexibility. Our data center solutions are tailored to our customers’ needs and delivered by our exceptional end-to-end team. Rowan is assembling a strategic portfolio of data center sites in Tier 1 markets across the United States at various stages of development, and we’re looking for incredible and passionate people to help us advance our company and our commitment to building a more sustainable future. Rowan is backed by Quinbrook, a leading investor in the energy transition, and Blackstone, the world’s largest alternative asset manager. Ready to join us in transforming the future of data centers and sustainability? Apply now to explore exciting career opportunities at Rowan Digital Infrastructure and be a part of our mission to revolutionize data center delivery. Role Summary Rowan Digital Infrastructure is looking for a Senior Associate, Regulatory Affairs & Public Policy - Texas to support the company’s Texas regulatory, legislative, and stakeholder engagement activities. This role will help advance Rowan’s Texas data center portfolio by supporting policy initiatives, regulatory engagement, stakeholder outreach, and project-level advocacy efforts that enable successful project development and operations. Working closely with Rowan's Regulatory Affairs & Public Policy Manager, the Senior Associate will help protect and advance Rowan's investments by supporting engagement with policymakers, regulators, industry associations, consultants, community organizations, and other key stakeholders. The role will contribute to the development and execution of Rowan's Texas policy strategy, support project-specific advocacy initiatives, and help translate complex legislative, regulatory, and market developments into actionable business recommendations. The ideal candidate will have a strong public policy foundation, excellent communication and organizational skills, comfort with ambiguity, and the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, cross-functional environment. Travel: Limited. Up to 10%-15% for company gatherings or to project sites. Location: Austin, TX Compensation: $105K - $125K (Offers Bonus) Essential Responsibilities Support Rowan's regulatory, legislative, and public policy activities across Texas, helping advance and protect the company's development and operational objectives. Assist with engagement before the Texas Legislature, Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUCT), ERCOT, local governments, economic development organizations, and other key stakeholders. Participate in meetings with elected officials, regulators, industry associations, consultants, utilities, and community stakeholders, helping prepare materials, coordinate follow-up actions, and advance Rowan's priorities. Represent Rowan at industry conferences, stakeholder meetings, community events, and other external forums as appropriate. Support project-level advocacy and stakeholder engagement efforts designed to facilitate project development and mitigate regulatory and policy risks. Analyze legislative, regulatory, and market developments affecting Rowan's Texas portfolio and communicate business impacts to cross-functional teams and leadership. Develop briefing materials, presentations, talking points, meeting summaries, and executive-ready memoranda to support internal and external engagement. Support Rowan's participation in ERCOT stakeholder processes, PUCT proceedings, trade associations, and industry coalitions. Build and maintain productive relationships with key stakeholders, including policymakers, regulators, economic development partners, consultants, and industry organizations. Support Rowan's energy, development, finance, legal, and economic development teams by identifying and assessing policy and regulatory risks and opportunities. Conduct research and analysis on issues affecting data center development, large load customers, electricity markets, taxation, economic development, and infrastructure investment. Track and monitor legislative, regulatory, and market developments relevant to Rowan's Texas portfolio and support internal reporting and risk assessment processes. Education, Skills, and Experience Bachelor’s degree and 3-6 years of experience in regulatory affairs, public policy, legislative affairs, government relations, or energy markets Direct experience with Texas energy policy and a solid understanding of PUCT regulations, proceedings, and regulatory processes - preferred Direct knowledge of ERCOT market structure, stakeholder processes, working groups, and governance - preferred Experience monitoring stakeholder discussions and providing real-time analysis, strategic recommendations, and action plans Experience analyzing legislation, regulatory proposals, market design changes, and policy developments Experience drafting testimony, comment letters, legislative analyses, bill revisions, advocacy materials, and executive briefings Ability to assess business, regulatory, and operational impacts and communicate recommendations to leadership Strong written and verbal communication skills with experience preparing executive-ready presentations, memos, and briefing materials Experience engaging with regulators, legislators, utilities, trade associations, industry groups, and other external stakeholders Preferred experience in electricity markets, utility regulation, power generation, oil and gas, water policy, environmental permitting, air emissions, or related infrastructure sectors Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced and highly cross-functional environment Fueled by Excellence & Collaboration At Rowan, we are a distributed team united by a common mission to transform data center delivery. Across our two offices, we offer a hybrid work environment supported by teamwork, technology, and in-office gathering time to help you be successful. We are headquartered in downtown Denver, Colorado and have an office in Seattle, Washington. Our team of talented and passionate individuals is spread out across the U.S. Here to support you At Rowan, we want to make sure you can do great work. We offer competitive benefits focused on helping you be and achieve your best. Equal Opportunity Employer Rowan Digital is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome and celebrate diversity in all aspects of our workforce. We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or any other legally protected status. We strive to create an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive.

item.title: Director Of State Government Affairs Texas Based
item.description: Description Fortune 100 information technology company seeks a Director of State Government Affairs, reporting to the Senior Director, State Government Affairs. This Director of State Government Affairs will work with corporate leadership and business units to represent company interests before state and local government officials to advance company policy priorities and other interests in Texas, including data center facilities. Responsibilities This role will support the company’s interests in Texas and adjacent states, as needed, while also supporting the broader state and local government affairs team. This includes representing company interests with third party groups and at events, monitoring state and local policy impacting the company, and maintaining a strong understanding of company operations to assess how external policy decision-making may impact business initiatives. The ideal candidate understands the importance of the role to the success of the organization; works well across teams; understands information technology across a broad range of business and policy priorities; and, is a self-starter who can manage multiple high-priority issues at once while driving results. QUALIFICATIONS / DESIRED SKILLS Minimum 5 years of experience in public policy at the state and local level with a thorough understanding of technology policy, and experience working with, serving, and influencing state and local government agencies. Relationships with Texas state and local officials, including executive and legislative branch, regulators and key energy stakeholders such as ERCOT and PUCT, municipal governments, and other relevant stakeholders. Understanding of technology policy and public policy issues affecting data center development, including tax, energy, land use, and economic development. Experience partnering with community engagement teams to build and strengthen a company’s presence in the communities where it operates and invests. The ability to align impact of state and local policy with business interests and develop and execute strategies to lead and shape complex initiatives and solutions. Ability to self-direct, including proven ability to prioritize, balance, and meet conflicting demands in a fast-paced environment with minimal supervision. Excellent written, oral communication and analytical skills with an ability to reduce complex terms and concepts into readily understandable concepts for policy makers. Experience briefing and staffing senior-level executives. Experience managing contract lobbyists and representing corporate interests with other external resources (e.g. consultants, trade associations). Excel at representing company at external facing policy and political events. Commitment to always acting with the highest integrity, including strict adherence to applicable laws and company values, which go beyond legal compliance. POSITION LOCATION: Austin, TX strongly preferred. Open to considering qualified candidate based in other Texas locations. TRAVEL COMPONENT: Approx. 20% travel may be required to be successful in this role MISC: This is a senior individual contributor role; no direct reports. #LI-NP4 Qualifications Disclaimer: Certain U.S. based or U.S. customer or client-facing roles may be required to comply with applicable requirements, such as immunization/occupational health mandates, and/or drug testing requirements. Range and benefit information provided in this posting are specific to the stated locations only US: Hiring Range in USD from: $102,300 to $209,500 per annum. May be eligible for bonus and equity. Medical, dental, and vision insurance, including expert medical opinion 2. Short term disability and long term disability 3. Life insurance and AD&D 4. Supplemental life insurance (Employee/Spouse/Child) 5. Health care and dependent care Flexible Spending Accounts 6. Pre-tax commuter and parking benefits 7. 401(k) Savings and Investment Plan with company match 8. Paid time off: Flexible Vacation is provided to all eligible employees assigned to a salaried (non-overtime eligible) position. Accrued Vacation is provided to all other employees eligible for vacation benefits. For employees working at least 35 hours per week, the vacation accrual rate is 13 days annually for the first three years of employment and 18 days annually for subsequent years of employment. Vacation accrual is prorated for employees working between 20 and 34 hours per week. Employees working fewer than 20 hours per week are not eligible for vacation. 9. 11 paid holidays 10. Paid sick leave: 72 hours of paid sick leave upon date of hire. Refreshes each calendar year. Unused balance will carry over each year up to a maximum cap of 112 hours. 11. Paid parental leave 12. Adoption assistance 13. Employee Stock Purchase Plan 14. Financial planning and group legal 15. item.title: Legislative Auditor Mid East Tennessee
item.description: Legislative Auditor: Mid-east Tennessee Location: Mid-east Tennessee (Putnam, Cumberland, White, Van Buren, Bledsoe, and Warren counties) Join us in our mission to make government work better. Role Snapshot This position conducts external audits for local government entities in the Mid-east Tennessee region, ensuring accountability, transparency, and effective operations across publicly funded organizations. Responsibilities may include examining and reviewing records, reports, financial statements, and management practices for state and local government entities and other organizations receiving public funds. Why You'll Love This Job Meaningful work that impacts communities across Tennessee Flexible schedules and a standard 37.5-hour workweek Opportunities for professional growth and development Collaborative and supportive team environment Comprehensive benefits and work-life balance What You'll Do Conduct audits of state and local governmental entities in accordance with professional auditing standards. Examine and review records, reports, financial statements, and management practices. Evaluate financial statement presentation, internal controls, compliance, and operational efficiency and effectiveness. Produce clear, logical, and well-supported workpapers and data analyses. Communicate clearly with auditees, coworkers, elected officials, and stakeholders. Take initiative, seek continuous improvement, and contribute to a collaborative team culture. What We're Looking For Required: Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Business Administration with at least 24 semester hours in accounting Ability to learn quickly, think critically, problem solve, and produce accurate work Strong attention to detail and organizational skills Clear written and verbal communication skills Ability to work tactfully with coworkers, auditees, and stakeholders Sound judgment in evaluating situations and making decisions Preferred: Certified Public Accountant (CPA) license (not required but strongly encouraged for advancement) Experience in auditing, governmental accounting, or related fields Logistics Travel: For Local Government Auditors, travel is required but is generally confined to same day commutes to and from a job site. Overnight stays may be required, as necessary. Compensation: Competitive salary and benefits, including annual and sick leave, insurance plans, pension, 401(k), college fee waivers, and flexible schedules. About the Office The Office of the Tennessee Comptroller of the Treasury audits state and local government entities and oversees financial and administrative management of state government. We are nationally recognized for professionalism and accountability and consistently rank as a Top Workplace. Learn more at www.comptroller.tn.gov Equal Opportunity Employer We are committed to fair and equal employment opportunities and maintaining a workplace free of discrimination and harassment. We prohibit discrimination based on race, color, national origin, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, pregnancy, religion, disability, veteran status, or any category protected by law. NOTICE This position requires a criminal background check. You may be required to provide information about your criminal history to be considered for this position. Texting TOS and Privacy Policy: Message type: informational; you will receive text messages regarding your application and potentially regarding interview scheduling. You can cancel the SMS service at any time. Just text "STOP" to the short code. After you send the SMS message "STOP" to us, we will send you an SMS message to confirm that you have been unsubscribed. After this, you will no longer receive SMS messages from us. If you want to join again, just sign up as you did the first time and we will start sending SMS messages to you again. If you are experiencing issues with the messaging program, you can reply with the keyword HELP for more assistance, or you can get help directly at ig.askhr@cot.tn.gov . Message frequency will vary depending on the application process. Carriers are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages. Msg & data rates may apply. If you have any questions about your text plan or data plan, it is best to contact your wireless provider. If you have any questions regarding privacy, please read our privacy policy below. Privacy Policy: We collect your mobile number and related opt-in data for the delivery of SMS messages. Your mobile opt-in data and consent will not be shared with third parties or affiliates for marketing or promotional purposes.

item.title: Office Assistant Iii Clark County Elections Office
item.description: Job Summary This position provides complex administrative support for the Elections division in the Auditor’s Office. Responsibilities include using all functions of the VoteWA statewide voter registration system; data entry; investigating and resolving required missing information on voter registration forms; scanning material into the voter registration system; working with State reports and other agencies to update voters’ status and address changes; issuing and receiving military and overseas electronic ballots; proofreading, issuing ballots; assisting with annexation and redistricting; assisting with signature verification; producing mailings to voters including military and overseas voters, and customer service.. This position will periodically require working overtime. This position is represented by Local 11 – OPEIU (Office and Professional Employees International Union, AFL-CIO). Due to the critical nature of the work, staff in Elections are considered essential to government services. This is not a remote working/telework position. Additionally, due to election deadlines, blackout dates may apply which restrict the use of vacation days at certain times of the year. This position is guaranteed 32 hours per week. Depending on departmental workload, operational needs, and Elections-related activity, the position may be scheduled for up to 40 hours per week. Qualifications Education and Experience: Three to five years of responsible and advanced administrative support experience including the full range of office and support functions; telephone and reception, word processing, spreadsheet and other personal computer applications, filing systems, mail, supplies, budgeting, accounting and others. The ideal candidate will have the following strengths: Prior experience working with elections Advanced proofreading abilities Ability to enter data accurately into the election management system Use advanced functions in Word and Excel Ability to manage multiple projects with changing priorities and deadlines Ability to work effectively with the public and staff of federal, state and local agencies Ability to work cooperatively in a high pressure team environment Excellent interpersonal communication skills Problem solving skills and ability to research data Demonstrated effective customer service experience Experience with and/or knowledge of state RCW’s, county codes, ordinances, and policies governing elections is desired Other combinations of education or experience, which would demonstrate the ability to perform the work, will be considered. Knowledge of : General office procedures and practices and of the specialized functions, policies, and procedures of the work unit; spelling, capitalization, punctuation and rules of grammar, and of the formats and clerical procedures used in performing the work; filing and record-keeping procedures; applicable laws, county codes, ordinances, and policies governing the work of the department and assignment; business English; PC computer applications such as word processing, spreadsheets and data bases; basic bookkeeping and/or cashiering methods and practices as required by the position. Ability to: Establish and maintain cooperative and effective working relationships; master the more complex department processes, services and functions; operate standard office equipment such as computer software applications, telephones, facsimile machines, copy machines; apply sound judgment in making decisions independently in accordance with established policies, procedures, and regulations; effectively maintain harmonious relationships with customers, including co-workers; diffuse difficult or highly charged situations; follow oral and written instructions; effectively guide and assist other employees; evaluate and improve department service delivery through enhancement of procedures, systems, organizational approaches and record keeping; develop and demonstrate effective customer service techniques; communicate effectively both orally and in written form. Examples of Duties Duties may include but are not limited to the following: Provides customer service to internal and external customers Provides direct customer service in the more complex service areas; assists lower level Office Assistants in researching and responding to difficult and detailed requests and situations from internal and external customers. Coordinates and completes a set of complex processes to support the work of internal customers; develops or recommends new processes, systems and work procedures. Coordinates the office operations of a function or service within the department of assignment. Researches, recommends and implements technical and/or administrative revisions to office systems, procedures and policies; interprets laws, regulations, policies and department procedures to the public and other staff. Assists with administrative tasks related to personnel, budgeting and facilities. Trains staff in the use of computer macros, templates, software, and data entry procedures, hardware and well as County department/division rules and regulations. Acts as project coordinator on major administrative projects. Implements new procedures and systems and trains staff. May provide lead direction to other administrative support staff; trains, assigns and assesses the work of assigned employees. May assume charge of support functions and staff in the absence of a leadworker or manager. Provides advanced administrative support. Develops and maintains databases for tracking departmental/program information; creates and produces complex reports from databases as required and necessary. Researches, interprets, prepares and maintains a variety of information and documents requiring knowledge of specific program requirements and terminology; creates written correspondence to customers regarding findings. Works with other departments, agencies or external contacts to research or coordinate work assignments. Compiles data, prepares documents and monitors expenditures to assist in the budget process. Researches and tracks information throughout the year. Composes and types complex detailed documents including letters, memos, minutes and other material from draft, dictation or general instructions. Proofreads and edits documents, presentation materials, brochures and other materials for grammar, clarity, punctuation and spelling; examines documents for completeness and accuracy. Gathers and compiles information and prepares reports and analyses in response to problems or as assigned. Uses spreadsheets to track, analyze and report quantitative information. Processes forms, applications, service requests and payments. Coordinates and organizes meetings, activities and functions; schedules rooms, assures notification of participants, arranges for necessary equipment and supplies. Performs related duties as required. SELECTION PROCESS If you wish to upload a resume or other documents: Resumes and documents must be attached together in the ‘Resume Upload’ section of the application. Multiple files are allowed, but all applicant attachments must be uploaded simultaneously, as there is no way to edit or append uploaded materials after submitting the application . Application Review (Pass/Fail) – An online application is required. Attaching a resume does not substitute for a completed application; incomplete applications will not pass the application review. Candidates deemed most qualified will be invited to participate in the remainder of the selection process. Practical Exam (Pass/Fail) – This recruitment may require a practical exam which will be job related and may include, but not be limited to, the qualifications outlined in the job announcement. Candidates deemed most qualified will be invited to participate in the remainder of the selection process. Oral Interview – The interview will be job related and may include, but not be limited to, the qualifications outlined in the job announcement. Top candidate(s) will continue in the process. Employment References will be conducted for the final candidates and may include verification of education. It is the general policy of the County that new employees should be hired at the lower steps of the applicable range and advance through the range at the normal progression. First review date: September18, 2026. This recruitment may close at any time on or after the first review date. Salary Grade Local 11.6 Salary Range $25.85 - $33.61- per hour Close Date Open Until Filled Recruiter Brianna Bradley (On Leave) Email: Brianna.Bradley@clark.wa.gov Equal Opportunity Employer Clark County is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal opportunity in employment, access, and delivery of all county services. Clark County’s Equal Employment Opportunity Plan is available at http://www.clark.wa.gov/human-resources/documents . Employee Benefits and additional compensation Clark County provides regular full-time and part-time employees with a comprehensive benefits package which includes medical, vision and dental insurance, paid leave, flexible spending accounts, life insurance and long-term disability, retirement, and deferred compensation. Some types of employees in some positions and bargaining units might have different benefits and additional compensation. More specific benefit information for the different bargaining units can be found at https://clark.wa.gov/human-resources/employee-benefits . Also please refer to the specific bargaining unit contract for additional compensation at https://clark.wa.gov/human-resources/documents . Retirement Information All Clark County employees must participate in a WASHINGTON STATE RETIREMENT SYSTEM PLAN (PERS, PSERS or LEOFF).Employee contributions begin the first day of work. Current contribution rates vary by plan but could range from 5% to 15% of gross pay, depending on the plan choice. For additional information, check out the Departm

item.title: Senior Director State Government Affairs
item.description: Job Description: As a privately-owned, biopharmaceutical company, Ferring pioneers and delivers life-changing therapies that help people build families and live better lives. Our independence helps us cultivate an entrepreneurial spirit and long-term perspective that enables us to achieve growth and scale, while remaining agile and true to our ‘people first’ philosophy. Built on a 70-year plus commitment to science and research, Ferring is relentless in its pursuit of science that drives powerful discoveries and therapies to help people build families, stay healthy, and stand up to the world’s oldest enemy: disease. The Senior Director, Government Affairs, State (Head) reports to Vice President, Government Affairs and Public Policy, and manages State Government Affairs and leads Ferring’s State Advocacy efforts. The Sr. Director, State Government Affairs is the lead and responsible for creating and sustaining relationships with state and local legislative offices. Both in Washington D.C. and in key states and districts, the Sr. Director identifies state policies that reflect and support Ferring’s strategy and growth agenda. This role must strictly comply with federal and state lobbying registration and conduct requirements. As well as internal compliance and company policy requirements. With Ferring, you will be joining a recognized leader, identified as one of “The World’s Most Innovative Companies” by Fast Company , and honored by Fortune with inclusion on its “Change the World List,” for addressing society’s unmet needs. Ferring US is also Great Places to Work® Certified, distinguishing it as one of the best companies to work for in the country. The Senior Director, Head of State Advocacy is responsible for developing and executing Ferring's state government affairs and advocacy strategy to advance business objectives, improve patient access, and support the company's public policy priorities. This role serves as the company's lead state advocacy expert and, where applicable, registered lobbyist, partnering across the organization and with external stakeholders to shape favorable legislative and regulatory outcomes. Key responsibilities include: Develop and execute state advocacy strategies that align with Ferring's business objectives, patient access goals, and public policy priorities. Partner with business leaders, Government Affairs colleagues, and cross-functional teams to identify advocacy priorities and deliver coordinated policy strategies. Monitor, analyze, and communicate legislative and regulatory developments, providing strategic guidance on risks, opportunities, and business implications. Lead state-based advocacy campaigns and influence legislative, regulatory, and reimbursement environments that impact patients, healthcare providers, and Ferring's therapeutic areas. Build and maintain trusted relationships with policymakers, regulators, governors, legislators, congressional delegations, advocacy organizations, healthcare stakeholders, coalition partners, trade associations, medical societies, and patient groups. Represent Ferring's interests before state government officials, industry organizations, and external stakeholders while elevating the company's reputation and visibility on key public policy issues. Identify and advance policy opportunities while proactively addressing legislative and regulatory challenges affecting the business. Serve as Ferring's lead representative and policy subject matter expert on state government affairs issues, providing timely insights on emerging trends and policy developments. Support and guide lobbying and advocacy efforts through policy analysis, strategic recommendations, messaging, stakeholder engagement, and coalition-building initiatives. Develop advocacy strategies that support product launches, market access objectives, and improved patient access and reimbursement outcomes. Prepare and deliver policy communications and advocacy materials, including briefing documents, legislative summaries, testimony, talking points, policy proposals, and stakeholder presentations. Prepare and support internal stakeholders for legislative meetings, hearings, formulary discussions, regulatory engagements, and other policy-related activities. Collaborate with public health organizations, academic institutions, patient advocates, prevention leaders, and community partners to advance public health objectives aligned with Ferring's mission. Lead the selection and management of external consultants, government relations firms, lobbying partners, and policy experts to support advocacy initiatives. Manage budgets, timelines, resources, and external partnerships to ensure effective execution of state advocacy priorities. Deliver actionable policy insights that inform business decisions, protect healthcare access, improve patient outcomes, and create enterprise value. Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s or Law degree preferred. Major in Government Relations, Public Administration, Public Relations or Political Science, Legal Studies, or commensurate experience in these or related area is preferred. 7+ years of progressively responsible experience in government affairs / relations at the local, state or federal level required; direct experience with policy issues affecting the life sciences industry with internal pharmaceutical company experience a plus. Understanding of legislative processes, including policy and budget processes, required; deep understanding preferred. Expert skills in research, evaluating and interpreting complex information. Understanding of customer service and customer relations, problem solving and tools for use in conflict management. A track record of success experience in life sciences with patient and professional organizations a plus. Strong knowledge of policy development methodologies and procedures required, experience in a Congressional office and/or with state legislators and Governors offices a plus. Demonstrated understanding and working knowledge of budgeting, budget management and projections for a government affairs function Effective written and oral communication skills required; experience in communications field a plus. Skilled in creating, preparing, reviewing and editing correspondence, reports, presentations and other assigned documents. Ability to influence and drive positive outcomes with Senior level Government officials & Stakeholders. Ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines. Ability to work independently, autonomously, proven ability to be self-directed, work with minimal supervision and accept responsibility. Ability to make sound judgments in reporting and interpreting data and information. Role will require travel up to 50% and is based out of the Washington D.C. market (office). Ferring + you At Ferring, we offer competitive total compensation along with an exceptional range of flexible benefits, personal support and tailored learning and development opportunities all designed to help you realize your full potential both in life and at work. From working hours that respect your lifestyle, a culture that is welcoming and equitable, and the chance to work with the industry’s most impressive people, these are just some of the ways we live our "People First" philosophy. Our Compensation and Benefits At Ferring, base salary is one part of our competitive total compensation and benefits package and is determined using a salary range. The base salary range for this role is $231,000 – $280,000, which is the reasonable estimate of the base compensation for this role. The actual amount paid may differ based on non-discriminatory factors such as experience, knowledge, skills, abilities, education and primary work location. Additional compensation for this role will be provided based on competitive annual incentive compensation targets in the form of an annual bonus - payouts are based on individual and company performance. Benefits for this role include: comprehensive healthcare (medical, dental, and vision) with a premium differential, inverse to base salary, to be paid by employees; a 401k plan and company match; short and long-term disability coverage; basic life insurance; wellness benefits; reimbursement for certain tuition expenses; sick time frontloaded yearly of 40 hours, or higher if state or local law requires; vacation time for full time employees to accrue between 112.5 and 150 hours yearly in the first four (4) years of employment, and additional accruals starting in the fifth (5th) year of employment; and 12 to 13 paid holidays per year. We are proud to offer 26 weeks of paid parental leave, learn more about the parental leave offering in our benefits package here . For roles that are not field-based, Ferring has a policy that allows employees to work up to two days from home and three at a Ferring site, weekly. Ferring is an equal opportunity employer. All aspects of employment will be based on merit, competence, performance, and business needs. We do not discriminate on the basis of gender, race, color, religion, marital status, age, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, pregnancy, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other status protected under federal, state, or local laws. Join our team and your voice will be heard, and your contributions will be valued. If you love to come up with new ways to make a positive difference and see them through, you will fit right in. We are proud to be an Affirmative Action/Equal Opportunity Employer (including Disability/Protected Veterans). We maintain a drug-free workplace. Location: Ferring Washington

item.title: U S State Government Affairs Manager
item.description: The application window is expected to close on: 10/05/2026 Location: Washington DC, most preferred Meet the Team Cisco is seeking a government affairs and public policy professional to join a global team as a U.S. State Government Affairs Manager. Reporting to the Vice President of State Government Affairs & Community Relations, this individual will help lead Cisco’s government engagements and public policy efforts across multiple states. Cisco’s Government Affairs team represents the company with governments around the world to build relationships with key leaders, advance Cisco’s public policy goals, and educate governments about our industry. Government Affairs is involved in all key legislative, regulatory, and global issues that impact the technology industry. We are comprised of government and public policy experts across two dozen countries who represent Cisco at the highest levels of government. The team has extensive experience in and out of government and are recognized leaders in the industry. Your Impact As a U.S. State Government Affairs Manager, you will develop and implement strategies to strengthen Cisco’s presence and influence with state government stakeholders and technology associations. In collaboration with internal teams—including People, Policy & Purpose (3P), Sales, Communications, Legal, and Product Development—you will drive innovative policy solutions that support Cisco’s business goals and mission to power an inclusive future for all. Key responsibilities include: Advising and preparing senior leaders for engagements with state and local officials, ensuring alignment with Cisco’s business objectives and overall strategy Monitoring, analyzing, and reporting on relevant state legislative, regulatory, and budget developments Building trusted relationships with legislators, legislative staff, governors’ offices, and state agencies to strengthen Cisco’s public sector leadership Educating policymakers on Cisco’s technology and its role in AI, cybersecurity, broadband access, economic development, and public safety Advancing policy priorities aligned with purpose-driven initiatives Representing Cisco in state-level hearings, meetings, and industry coalitions Drafting and presenting testimony, position papers, and advocacy materials Minimum Qualifications: 7+ years of political and public policy experience in government, corporate government affairs, public affairs, trade associations, or public policy institutions Strong understanding of legislative and regulatory processes related to technology policy and familiarity with public policy issues affecting the technology industry Excellent political judgment and relationship-building skills Strong communication, writing, collaboration, and advocacy abilities with a demonstrated ability to build consensus across internal teams in pursuit of shared objectives Ability to travel throughout the U.S. and, on occasion, internationally Preferred Qualifications: Experience in state and local government relations, government affairs, public policy, public affairs, political campaigns, lobbying, outreach, or research Proven success leading policy or public affairs initiatives, such as lobbying or advocacy campaigns Extensive experience driving cross-functional collaboration with senior stakeholders and influencing decisions at all organizational levels Skilled in managing executives with exceptional leadership, communication, and collaboration skills Deep knowledge of technology policy and commitment to Cisco’s vision of a secure and accessible Internet Demonstrated ability to integrate public policy with business strategy and corporate development objectives Why Cisco? At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint. Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere. We are Cisco, and our power starts with you. Message to applicants applying to work in the U.S. and/or Canada: The starting salary range posted for this position is $161,300.00 to $204,800.00 and reflects the projected salary range for new hires in this position in U.S. and/or Canada locations, not including incentive compensation*, equity, or benefits. Individual pay is determined by the candidate's hiring location, market conditions, job-related skillset, experience, qualifications, education, certifications, and/or training. The full salary range for certain locations is listed below. For locations not listed below, the recruiter can share more details about compensation for the role in your location during the hiring process. U.S. employees are offered benefits, subject to Cisco’s plan eligibility rules, which include medical, dental and vision insurance, a 401(k) plan with a Cisco matching contribution, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability coverage, and basic life insurance. Please see the Cisco careers site to discover more benefits and perks. Employees may be eligible to receive grants of Cisco restricted stock units, which vest following continued employment with Cisco for defined periods of time. U.S. employees are eligible for paid time away as described below, subject to Cisco’s policies: 10 paid holidays per full calendar year, plus 1 floating holiday for non-exempt employees 1 paid day off for employee’s birthday, paid year-end holiday shutdown, and 4 paid days off for personal wellness determined by Cisco Non-exempt employees** receive 16 days of paid vacation time per full calendar year, accrued at rate of 4.92 hours per pay period for full-time employees Exempt employees participate in Cisco’s flexible vacation time off program, which has no defined limit on how much vacation time eligible employees may use (subject to availability and some business limitations) 80 hours of sick time off provided on hire date and each January 1st thereafter, and up to 80 hours of unused sick time carried forward from one calendar year to the next Additional paid time away may be requested to deal with critical or emergency issues for family members Optional 10 paid days per full calendar year to volunteer For non-sales roles, employees are also eligible to earn annual bonuses subject to Cisco’s policies. Employees on sales plans earn performance-based incentive pay on top of their base salary, which is split between quota and non-quota components, subject to the applicable Cisco plan. For quota-based incentive pay, Cisco typically pays as follows: .75% of incentive target for each 1% of revenue attainment up to 50% of quota; 1.5% of incentive target for each 1% of attainment between 50% and 75%; 1% of incentive target for each 1% of attainment between 75% and 100%; and Once performance exceeds 100% attainment, incentive rates are at or above 1% for each 1% of attainment with no cap on incentive compensation. For non-quota-based sales performance elements such as strategic sales objectives, Cisco may pay 0% up to 125% of target. Cisco sales plans do not have a minimum threshold of performance for sales incentive compensation to be paid. The applicable full salary ranges for this position, by specific state, are listed below: New York City Metro Area: $173,400.00 - $265,200.00 Non-Metro New York state & Washington state: $161,300.00 - $235,500.00 * For quota-based sales roles on Cisco’s sales plan, the ranges provided in this posting include base pay and sales target incentive compensation combined. ** Employees in Illinois, whether exempt or non-exempt, will participate in a unique time off program to meet local requirements.
