item.title: Legislative And Regulatory Research Intern
item.description: At Fried Frank, we’re a community of 800 lawyers and 500 business services professionals across New York, Washington, DC, London, Frankfurt, and Brussels. We advise leading corporations, investment funds, and financial institutions on high-stakes M&A, securities, regulatory matters, real estate, and litigation. Our culture is grounded in our core values — excellence, integrity and collaboration — and is designed to foster continuous learning, meaningful mentorship, and lasting professional growth. We are firmly committed to pro bono service and social justice, building on a proud legacy in civil rights. Our inclusive talent strategy is a core part of our broader talent management efforts and we remain steadfast in fostering a workplace where everyone has the opportunity to grow, thrive, and become their best professional and personal selves. Our business services professionals are integral to the firm’s success, driving innovation, operational excellence and exceptional client service across all areas of the firm. We offer competitive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package, including comprehensive medical coverage, retirement plans and health and wellness initiatives designed to support your personal and professional wellbeing. We welcome passionate, driven individuals to join us, and be part of a team where you’ll be supported, inspired and empowered to build an exceptional career. Position Summary : The firm is seeking a motivated college student, grad student or recent graduate for a paid internship supporting our Legislative Research Attorney. This role is ideal for a student considering law librarianship, law school or a career as a paralegal, offering direct, hands-on exposure to how attorneys and legislative professionals track, analyze, and organize legal and regulatory developments to service clients. The intern will work closely with the Legislative Research Attorney and other staff and will gain practical experience with government publications, legal databases, AI tools, and document management systems used in a law firm practice. Duties & Responsibilities: Daily Federal Register and Congressional Record monitoring. Review and flag items relevant to the firm's clients and practice areas. Careful, daily reading provides hands on learning about the legislative and regulatory processes and allows for connections to be made beyond simple keyword alerts. Legislative and Regulatory transcript summaries. Using the latest legal AI tools, prepare and validate clear, concise summaries of bills, rules and congressional and agency hearing transcripts for use by attorneys and clients. Learn how to read and understand legislative and regulatory texts. Bill tagging in BGOV and StateNet. Accurately tag and categorize federal and state legislation within BGOV and StateNet tracking platforms. This work is detail-intensive but essential to keeping the firm's legislative tracking systems reliable. Legislative history (LH) folder construction in iManage. Assist with an ongoing project to build and organize legislative history folders in iManage, ensuring research materials and legislative histories are properly filed, searchable, and easily accessible to attorneys. Online legislative history pages. Help maintain and build out intranet pages to host legislative histories for significant bills. Create and update links back to the underlying materials in iManage. News and publication monitoring. Monitor business and legal news publications for developments relevant to the firm's clients and practice areas. Support the Legislative Research Attorney’s work in circulating relevant items to each team. Legal database research. Conduct research using legal and legislative databases to support ongoing monitoring projects. Education / Experience : Currently enrolled in an undergraduate degree or graduate degree program; students considering law librarianship, law school or a paralegal career are especially encouraged to apply. Interest in government, public policy, or law is a plus. Skills & Abilities : Strong reading comprehension and attention to detail. Prior exposure to complex legislative and regulatory texts is a plus. Excellent written communication skills, particularly the ability to summarize material clearly and concisely. Highly organized, reliable, and comfortable with repetitive, detail-oriented tasks that require sustained accuracy. Research capability, though no prior experience with BGOV, StateNet, or iManage is required; training will be provided. The actual salary offered will be based on a number of factors including but not limited to the qualifications of the applicant, years of relevant experience, level of education attained, certifications or other professional licenses held, and if applicable, the location in which the applicant lives and/or from which they will be performing the job. Washington DC Salary Range $20 - $20 USD

item.title: Election Support Contractor
item.description: We support democracy. Our vision at Election Systems & Software (ES&S) is simple and unwavering — we provide products and services of exceptional quality and value to maintain voter confidence and enhance the voting experience. We accomplish this through continuous investments in research and development, resulting in regular product updates and security enhancements for each voting system we design, build, sell, and support. Join the ES&S team where we are crafting the future of voting in the United States! As part of our team, you will provide solutions that meet the industry’s ever-evolving needs. Our people apply their innovative perspective to challenges big and small, and ES&S provides the resources to make our employees’ vision a reality. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Varying length assignment working with a team to accomplish specific tasks in support of upcoming elections. Work onsite at customer location performing assigned tasks. Equipment Testing - Follow a checklist of actions and procedures to produce output to verify accuracy. Detailed training will be provided for all testers. All testing will take place in a warehouse-type environment. Election Support - Provide technical support and customer service during the election. Report to the Account Manager with progress updates and issues as required. Maintain a positive work environment and positive customer relationships. This job description is not intended to be a comprehensive listing of all activities, duties, or responsibilities required of the employee in this role. Activities, duties, or responsibilities may change at any time with or without notice. Qualifications: Technical capacity, problem-solving, analysis, strong communication skills, strong interpersonal skills Well-developed commitment to customer service and a passion for quality over quantity Professional appearance and personal effectiveness/credibility Location Candidates must live in Philadelphia Pay Work Environment: While performing the duties of this job, the employee may be exposed to moving Electro/mechanical parts and noise. This position may require travel in a variety of weather conditions. Physical Demands: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. The employee must be able to lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to stand, walk, hands to finger, handle or feel; and reach with hands and arms. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus. Security: Required to consistently demonstrate adherence to all security requirements and accepted practices as contained in the current ES&S Security Policy. Incumbents must proactively read, comprehend and adhere to all ES&S security policies, practices and procedures regarding the safety and safekeeping of co-workers, products, services and other intellectual property as defined in the ES&S New Business and Non-disclosure, or Proprietary matters, Confidential matters and Non-Competition agreements, and the current ES&S Security Policy Manual. EEO Statement: In order to provide equal employment and advancement opportunities to all individuals, employment decisions at ES&S will be based on merit, qualifications, and abilities. ES&S does not discriminate in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of race, creed, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship status, marital status, age, disability, genetic information, or because of past, current, or future military obligations or any other characteristics protected by law.This policy governs all aspects of employment, including selection, job assignment, compensation, discipline, termination, and access to benefits and training.

item.title: Legislative Photographer
item.description: Job Posting Title Legislative Photographer Agency 423 LEGISLATIVE SERVICE BUREAU Supervisory Organization Legislative Service Bureau–State Capitol Job Posting End Date Refer to the date listed at the top of this posting, if available. Continuous if date is blank. Note: Applications will be accepted until 11:59 PM on the day prior to the posting end date above. Estimated Appointment End Date (Continuous if Blank) Full/Part-Time Full time Job Type Regular Compensation Salary Range: $45,000 - $48,000 Job Description Overview: The Legislative Service Bureau is seeking a skilled and creative photographer to join our team, which provides a range of photography services to the members of the Oklahoma Legislature. Photographers document the business of State government throughout legislative sessions, take official State portraits, capture special events, and document historical moments. The ideal candidate for this role has strong technical skills, the ability to adapt quickly, is customer-service oriented, and works well in a team. Primary Responsibilities: Photography: Take high-quality photographs of state legislators, government officials, events, and activities within the Capitol and its surroundings. Event Coverage: Document legislative sessions, committee meetings, and other significant events held at the Capitol. Portrait Photography: Capture professional portraits of lawmakers, executives, and distinguished guests as required. Art and Architectural Elements of the Capitol: Capture and showcase the art and the building in a visually compelling and accurate manner. Archival Work: Organize and maintain an extensive photo archive of Capitol events and historical moments for future reference and historical documentation. Collaboration: Coordinate with government officials, communications teams, and event organizers to ensure photography needs are met effectively. Editing and Post-Production: Edit and retouch photographs as needed to ensure high quality and adherence to established standards. Publication Support: Provide photographs for use in official publications, reports, social media, and other communication channels. Image Printing: Manage the printing and distribution of high-quality images for legislators, ensuring timely delivery and adherence to specified requirements for official use and personal requests. Skills and Qualifications: Proven experience as a professional photographer, ideally with experience in event coverage and portrait photography. Proficiency in digital photography and photo editing software (e.g., Adobe Photoshop, Lightroom, ACDSee). Strong understanding of composition, lighting, and visual storytelling. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Ability to work independently and manage time effectively, especially during fast-paced events. Flexibility to work evening hours during session as needed. Knowledge of state government operations and legislative processes (preferred but not required). Education and Certification: Bachelor’s degree or certification in Photography, Visual Arts, Journalism, or a related field is preferred. Equivalent professional experience may be considered. Working Conditions: The role is primarily based at the Oklahoma State Capitol in Oklahoma City. Will require standing for extended periods during events. Traversing multiple sets of stairs daily with limited use of elevators Sitting for extended periods of time while editing photos Application Process: Interested candidates should submit a resume, portfolio showcasing relevant work, and a cover letter outlining their qualifications and interest in the position. Equal Opportunity Employment The State of Oklahoma is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of genetic information, race, religion, color, sex, age, national origin, or disability. Current active State of Oklahoma employees must apply for open positions internally through the Workday Jobs Hub . If you are needing any extra assistance or have any questions relating to a job you have applied for, please click the link below and find the agency for which you applied for additional information: Agency Contact

item.description: Design & Selections Coordinator Sineath Construction Weaverville, North Carolina, United States Full-time 3 days ago $55,000 - $65,000 USD yearly Sineath Construction Weaverville, NC | Full-Time | In-Office About the Role Sineath Construction is looking for an organized, design-minded coordinator to support our Designer and Purchasing & Estimating team through the residential selection and pre-construction process. This role is a strong fit for an early-career interior designer who understands residential design and enjoys bringing structure to a project. You will help clients move from selections to approved specifications while keeping information, budgets, vendors, and deadlines aligned for the field team. Coordinate client selection deadlines, approvals, specifications, and supporting documentation. Post and maintain accurate selection information in JobTread so clients, vendors, and field staff can easily follow the latest information. Communicate with clients, vendors, and trade partners through JobTread and other appropriate channels. Maintain selection reports and finish schedules for completeness, clarity, and team visibility. Track selection impacts on project budgets and update budget information after approvals. Coordinate selection-related purchase orders and help ensure materials are ordered and available when scheduled. Maintain vendor and trade partner information and support annual agreement and setup requirements. Assist with selection-related estimating tasks and variance purchase orders as needed. Track product rebate opportunities and help keep project records organized and current. Provide responsive client and partner communication throughout the selection process. What We're Looking For Degree or formal training in Interior Design, or approximately 2 years of relevant interior design experience. Residential design experience or a strong understanding of residential finishes, materials, and selections. Strong organizational and project coordination skills with excellent follow-through. Ability to manage multiple deadlines, details, vendors, and client requests at the same time. Clear, professional communication skills and a collaborative approach. Comfort working with budgets, specifications, and project documentation. Proficiency with Microsoft Office. Experience with JobTread, Bluebeam, Chief Architect, AutoCAD, SoftPlan, or similar design/project management software is a plus. Ability to work independently, make sound decisions, and ask for direction when needed. What Success Looks Like Selection information is accurate, current, and easy for clients and field staff to use. Client selections and approvals are completed by established deadlines. Selection-related orders are coordinated accurately and on time. Budget impacts and project documentation are kept current. Clients, vendors, designers, and field staff receive clear and timely communication. Compensation & Benefits Salary: $55,000-$65,000 annually , depending on experience. Full-time, in-person position with typical office hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday. Medical Insurance : Eligible after 90 days Paid Time Off : 5 days/year (Years 1-2); 10 days/year after 2 years Sick Leave : 5 days/year 401(k) : Eligible after 1 year with company match (100% match on the first 3%; 50% on the next 2%) How to Apply Please submit your resume and a brief summary of your residential design or selections experience. Candidates with a portfolio or examples of residential design work may include those materials with their application. Weaverville, North Carolina, United States $55,000 - $65,000 USD yearly

item.title: Legislative Clerk House Of Representatives Democrat Office
item.description: Description DESCRIPTION OF WORK: North Carolina’s House of Representatives is seeking a highly qualified professional to work as a Legislative Clerk in a Democratic Legislator’s office. Legislative Clerks assist Legislators, also known as Legislative “Members” of the House, in fulfilling their public obligations by providing support services in the areas of administration, communication, research, and public relations. This position requires a high level of organization and accountability as well as the ability to perform independently and maintain composure in a fast-paced, dynamic environment. This position is a permanent, full-time position. Days of work are typically Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. However, when the House of Representatives is in session, evening work may be necessary on Monday through Thursday and occasionally weekend work may be required as the job duties demand, based on the needs of the Representative. This position is under the direct supervision of the Representative and has no direct supervisory responsibilities, unless requested by the Member to assist in the supervision of an Intern. Examples of Duties ( The Legislative Clerk will be given a wide range of tasks, projects, and duties, including, but not limited to, the following) : Conducting research into various public policy issues Office management, email, and calendar management Drafting correspondence and constituent newsletter Coordinating with other legislators and staff on policy initiatives and legislation Coordinating with state agency liaisons to fulfill constituent requests On-boarding, training, and managing Interns Creating and monitoring communication strategies for the Representative Identifying and monitoring district specific issues Other items related to the Representative's official duties Other tasks assigned by the Representative KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES/COMPETENCIES: Ability to present information clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing Practical knowledge of the elements of reference and policy research Proficiency with all Microsoft Office applications, research software, and Adobe Acrobat DC Ability to maintain composure and work cooperatively under pressure with legislators, legislative staff, and the public on a daily basis Ability to work independently, organize and analyze materials, and prioritize tasks Ability to maintain confidentiality and to handle politically sensitive work Ability to work objectively and impartially both with respect to members of both political parties and with respect to issues of state Willingness and ability to work extended schedules MINIMUM EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS: Required Education and Experience: Undergraduate degree; or an equivalent combination of education and experience Preference will be given to those with the following : Outstanding record of academic achievement Strong record of leadership in an academic, professional, and/or extracurricular setting SUPPLEMENTAL AND CONTACT INFORMATION: Instructions: To apply for the Legislative Clerk position, please complete the online NC General Assembly application through the NC General Assembly website: https://careers.ncleg.gov/ . Required Supporting Documents: Please Note the Following: Application must be completed in its entirety, including detailed education and work history. Résumés are not accepted in lieu of the NC General Assembly Application. Incomplete packets will not be considered. Agency Contact Information: North Carolina General Assembly - House of Representatives Office of House of Representatives Laura.Bone@ncleg.gov ***Due to the high volume of applications received, we are unable to provide information regarding the status of your application.***

item.title: Elections Deputy Director
item.description: Elections Deputy Director Craven County New Bern, North Carolina, United States Full-time 23 days ago $62,341 - $62,341 USD yearly Primary Purpose The Elections Deputy Director works under the general supervision of the Elections Director. The Elections Deputy Director performs professional, managerial, and administrative work for the Board of Elections and carries out all duties or responsibilities as assigned by the Elections Director. Reports to the Elections Director of the Craven County Board of Elections. Essential Functions Assist the Director in the administration of all functions of the office of the Board of Elections to comply with General Statutes, mandates and directives by the Executive Director of the North Carolina State Board of Elections in order to effectively comply with North Carolina election laws. Ensures compliance with all State and County issued cyber security directives, including cyber security and physical security. And adhere to the duties delegated to the county boards of elections in NCGS 163-33. Assist the Director in organizing and preparing for all elections and recounts, including preparing ballots, programming, and testing of voting machines; coordinating delivery of voting equipment, signs, and supplies to voting places; and arranging return of these items Ensures testing of voting equipment for accuracy of tabulation and function prior to elections and conducts post-election certification processes. Assist the Director in preparing personnel, payroll, and finance paperwork. Assist the Director in preparation of the annual budget and budget amendments. Assist the Director in organizing and supervising procedures and methods of receiving and processing applications for voter registration, including ascertaining that applicants are eligible to register in the county; ensures that voter registration records are updated to reflect changes of address, name changes and changes of party affiliation, including mailing out required notices for new registrations and changes to registration records. Supervises the removal of ineligible voters. Provides lists of voters requested by political parties, candidates, the general public and others. Maintains custody of voter registration and other records in a safe and secure manner and location. Assist the Director in identifying the number of voting places required and recommend locations; assist in negotiating usage as needed. Assist the Director in coordinating Board meetings and preparing copies of reports for the Board. Assigns, directs and supervises activities of the Election Specialists, Elections Technician and all part time and temp positions. through direct supervision, ensuring adherence to established policies, procedures and standards. Assists and advises subordinates in resolving problems as non-routine situations arise. Assist or makes recommendations for routine personnel matters affecting subordinates, including interviewing applicants, hiring, assigning, scheduling, evaluating, promoting, disciplining, dismissing, etc. Perform related tasks as assigned. Minimum Education and Experience Work experience in North Carolina elections at the County staff level. Graduation from a four-year college or university and three (3) years of experience in the planning and management of a business or governmental program or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Two (2) years of experience as an Elections Deputy Director preferred. Special Requirements: Must be certified or obtain certification as a North Carolina Elections Administrator from the State Board of Elections within three years of appointment. Driving is an essential function of this position. To be considered, you must have a valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record. If your driver’s license is from another state, you will be required to obtain and show proof of a valid NC driver’s license within 60 days of hire. Background check is required. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities: Thorough knowledge of North Carolina General Statutes and Board of Election guidelines governing elections. Thorough knowledge of principles and practices of election programs and related laws, ordinances, standards, and regulations. Considerable knowledge of the State Election Information Management system software. Considerable knowledge of the State Election Information Management System software. Ability to direct staff, plan for and allocate resources, interpret policies and regulations. Ability to direct voter registration, election voting procedures, record keeping and reporting of programs and services Ability to develop and maintain cooperative internal and external Departmental relationships. Ability to represent program in written form and effectively communicate with others. Considerable knowledge of modern office practices, procedures, and equipment. Working knowledge of the operations and functions of County government. Skill in computer operations and related equipment. Ability to develop and maintain effective working relationships with election officials, elected officials, news media, county officials, Board members, other employees, and the general public. Attend required and mandated trainings, meetings, and conferences by the NC State Board of Elections and others approved by the Board. Additional Information May be required to serve the County during times of disaster. New Bern, North Carolina, United States $62,341 - $62,341 USD yearly

item.title: Franklin County Election Canvasser
item.description: The Opportunity Down Home North Carolina (DHNC) seeks field canvassers in Franklin County to aid in our 2026 field campaigns. This year, Down Home members will endorse multiple candidates for office who align with our values and vision for a North Carolina that works for all working folks. Down Home is working to engage voters in our small towns this year to inform them about the upcoming elections, when, where, and how they can vote, and recruit more folks into our movement. Opportunities are available in the following counties: Ashe, Alamance, Cabarrus, Chatham, Franklin, Granville, Iredell, Johnson, Nash, Orange, Person, Pitt, Randolph, Rowan, Rockingham, Vance, Watauga, and Wilson. The ideal candidate is a people-person motivated to build a powerful multiracial base that wins changes for poor and working-class people in rural North Carolina. They have excellent listening skills, are team players and independent workers, and are aligned with Down Home's mission. The Work Have conversations with community members through door-to-door canvassing Participate in 4 to 6 canvasses per week Ensure that data and information collection are consistent and accurate Troubleshooting issues within the program Must be willing to work in a team-centered environment. Required Traits Excellent communication and listening skills: Can engage deeply with people they have just met. Be able to listen to community members and understand their concerns. Can build rapport quickly and is comfortable having relational conversations. Team player: Contribute to a growing and fast-paced team. Take directions well and be willing to offer feedback and suggestions to co-workers and management. Offer support to teammates and ask for help when needed. Independent worker: Be able to complete multiple canvass shifts a week. Meet deadlines and hit metric goals. Ensure that numbers are reported on time with data integrity at the top of mind. Attention to detail and be able to provide thoughtful solutions to problems that arise. Be able to work in a fast-paced environment where work areas are expected to change frequently. Mission alignment: Committed to the vision of a powerful, inclusive, rural, multiracial, working-class movement-building as a path towards liberation for all people. Is aligned with the idea that building power takes both election programs and long-term base-building and community investment. Compensation Compensation for this contract position is $22 hourly. Hours are flexible, with shifts available during the afternoon and evening. This role is not eligible for employee-sponsored benefits or healthcare. Applicants must be able and willing to travel regularly for work. How to Apply Applications will be accepted on a rolling basis if spots are available. We will still accept applications if this job description is posted on Down Home’s website (www.downhomenc.org).

item.title: Assistant Professor Of Political Science Methods And American Politics
item.description: Assistant Professor of Political Science (Methods and American Politics) Transylvania University ( www.transy.edu ) invites applications for a 9-month, tenure-track position in Political Science, beginning August 25, 2027. The political science program at Transylvania University emphasizes hands-on experiential learning. Students learn by engaging the real world; completing internships and mentorships with policymakers and practitioners; participating in active learning in the classroom; and completing in-depth research projects focused on addressing complex societal challenges. The program stresses the cultivation of good analytic skills through reading, writing, research and presentations. Why Join Transylvania University? Founded in 1780, Transylvania University is one of the nation’s oldest institutions. Ranked in the Top 100 Best Liberal Arts colleges for 2025 by Niche, we’re a vibrant campus in the heart of Lexington, Kentucky full of curious minds, creative energy, and people who genuinely love what they do. We are mentors and community builders who help shape the next generation of thinkers, creators and leaders. We cultivate independent thinking, open-mindedness, creative expression and commitment to lifelong learning and social responsibility in a diverse world. With approximately 1,000 students, Transylvania is a student-centered institution with small class sizes. We offer additional opportunities for travel and team-taught courses, and a focus on experiential learning. Who are we looking for? Eligible candidates will have a Ph.D. in Political Science or a related field by the start date. The successful candidate will have expertise in quantitative methods and in areas of American politics other than public law. Applicants with an interest in American political behavior, and those with undergraduate teaching experience (particularly in research methods), are particularly encouraged to apply. This person will jointly serve the Political Science program and Data Analytics minor and be responsible for developing and expanding our interdisciplinary minor in Data Analytics as well as broadening the utilization of quantitative research methods across campus. The successful candidate will have a commitment to teaching, value interdisciplinary dialogue, and work collaboratively with other faculty. The teaching load consists of three courses per term, plus one short-term course in May term (3-3-1). Responsibilities include: Teach Introduction to Data Analytics and Statistics; Data Acquisition, Wrangling and Visualization; and topics within their area of specialization in Political Science. Contributions to teaching core classes such as Political Analysis and Senior Seminar are expected, along with occasional supervision of community internships and independent research. Regular contributions to First-Year programing and service as an academic adviser. Other responsibilities include academic scholarship/professional activity, preferably involving undergraduate students, and service to the university through various committee appointments. How do you apply? Qualified candidates should submit a single PDF including: a cover letter curriculum vitae statement of teaching philosophy statement of research philosophy unofficial graduate transcripts list of at least three professional references The successful candidate will be asked to provide official graduate transcripts and be subject to a background check. Send questions specific to this search to Dr. Steve Hess, search committee chair, at shess@transy.edu. Transylvania University is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is committed to enhancing the diversity of the university community. In support of this goal, we embrace diversity and encourage applications from qualified candidates with a wide range of backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences.

item.title: Associate Professor Of Political Science Oklahoma Baptist University
item.description: OBU Mission Statement OBU transforms lives by equipping students to pursue academic excellence, integrate faith with all areas of knowledge, engage a diverse world, and live worthy of the high calling of God in Christ. Expectations for all Employees Oklahoma Baptist University achieves its mission through a shared commitment to the following expectations. All employees must embrace these expectations and model them in their behavior. Demonstrate commitment to the essentials of the Christian faith. Commit to the mission and vision of Oklahoma Baptist University. Treat people with dignity and respect. Build relationships on honesty, integrity, and trust. Strive for excellence through teamwork, leadership, and a strong work ethic. Manage human and financial resources wisely and efficiently. Purpose: Oklahoma Baptist University invites applications for an Assistant or Associate Professor of Political Science position (beginning August 2026). Area of specialization is open. The successful candidate will be required to teach American National Government and Introduction to Political Science, as well as courses on congress, courts, and U.S. presidency. They may also teach other courses in the catalog or develop new courses that align with their interests and background, with prior approval. The standard load is 24 credit hours per academic year. In addition to teaching, the successful candidate will advise political science majors and minor with their course and career options. Candidates must be committed to the mission of OBU as a Christian liberal arts university. PhD in Political Science preferred (advanced ABD considered). Essential Functions: · Teach introductory and upper-level undergraduate Political Science courses. · Serve as an advisor to Political Science majors and minors. · Keep accurate class records and submit reports and grades. · Work regularly with faculty members from other disciplines. · Keep regular office hours for advising students. · Be an active member in a local evangelical church. Other Duties: · Maintain an active program of professional development. · Serve on university committees and take an active part in shaping the work of the division. · Assist in recruiting students to the Political Science program. · Support and guide students in research and practical. Required Qualifications: · Must be able to teach multiple Political Science courses, including ones covering the major branches of government. · Possess and demonstrate strong interpersonal skills, communication skills, and pedagogy. · Be able to conduct a college classroom to maximize the student learning experience. · Be able to adjust teaching methods to meeting student needs. · Be able to work effectively with college students in either individual advisement, as well as small and large class environments. · Be able to relate to colleagues in the OBU community as well as be a representative to the professional community beyond OBU. · Be proficient in office technology, office software (including various Microsoft tools), and classroom presentation software. Education: · Required : PhD in Political Science (advanced ABD considered). · Preferred : PhD in Political Science. Experience: · Preferred: Experience teaching undergraduate in a Christian, liberal arts environment. Special Requirements: · Must be a member of a local evangelical* Christian church. *Evangelical is a broad term referring to segment within Christianity which maintains the authority of the Bible and the belief in salvation by faith in Jesus alone. OBU Benefits Summary: OBU understands that our employees are our most valuable assets when fulfilling our mission. We strive to offer an extensive array of benefits and opportunities for employees to choose from. Full-time employees benefit from the generous OBU provision of premium contributions for nationwide family-friendly Health and Dental coverages along with free life insurance that includes accidental death and dismemberment equal to an employee’s base salary. OBU provides access to optional employee-paid ancillary benefits like vision, hospitalization, critical illness, accident, additional employee-paid family life insurance coverages, and education benefits at OBU and other institutions of higher education. There is generous paid time off that includes annual granted vacation time, accrued sick leave, six annual holidays, and week-long breaks for Thanksgiving and Christmas that include energy conservation days. For all employees working at least half-time, there is an employer matching opportunity for retirement investments in a 403(b)(9) plan administered by Guide Stone. There are numerous other perks and opportunities for OBU employees including FREE family membership to the OBU Recreation and Wellness Center or RAWC, Global outreach university mission trips, cafeteria discounts, and parking privileges to name a few.

item.title: Election Specialist Voting Location Workforce Services
item.description: Election Specialist - Voting Location & Workforce Services Johnson County Kansas Olathe, Kansas, United States Full-time 11 days ago Overview A career with Johnson County Government is more than just a job, it is an opportunity to serve a diverse and expanding community in meaningful ways. We challenge ourselves to be a different kind of government because we care deeply about our community and each other. Committed to our shared values, we provide excellent public service, seeking always to improve ourselves and our organization. We offer wonderful benefits, retirement plans, wellness incentives, a great organizational culture, and much more! If you’re searching for something more than just a job, something akin to a calling, then consider the challenge and opportunity of being a member of Johnson County Government! This position will close on Tuesday, September 29th, 2026. Job Description Be part of the team that makes voting possible in Johnson County! This Election Specialist position is part of our Polling Location and Workforce Services team, which leads the effort to recruit and support election workers and identify and survey potential voting locations. We’re looking for someone who enjoys working with people, takes pride in excellent customer service, and can stay organized and adaptable in a fast-paced environment where every detail matters. Success in this role requires strong communication, dependability, flexibility, attention to detail, and a commitment to providing professional, nonpartisan service to Johnson County voters. Essential Duties: Election Operations Support: Assists in the preparation and execution of election activities, including early voting and election day operations. Supports operational readiness to ensure polling locations and election processes function effectively. Election Worker Coordination: Supports recruitment, assignment, communication, and coordination of election workers. Assists with staffing updates and helps ensure polling locations are adequately staffed. Training Support: Assists in the coordination and delivery of election worker training programs, including preparation of materials, scheduling, and tracking attendance and completion. Logistics and Equipment Support: Assists with preparation, staging, deployment, and retrieval of voting equipment and supplies. Supports warehouse operations and inventory management as assigned. Voting Equipment and Testing Support: Assists with election system preparation, including support for election programming, Logic & Accuracy (L&A) testing, and equipment verification, as assigned. Data Entry and Record Maintenance: Maintains accurate records across systems, including voter data, election worker information, assignments, and operational documentation. Ensures data integrity and completeness. Customer Service and Communication: Serves as a point of contact for voters, candidates, election workers, and internal staff. Responds to inquiries and provides timely, accurate information, escalating issues as needed. Cross-Division Coordination: Works collaboratively across divisions to support election operations, ensuring alignment between workforce, logistics, technology, and voter services. Confidentiality and Discretion: Handles sensitive and confidential information with a high degree of discretion, ensuring appropriate handling and security of information. Job Requirements Minimum Job Requirements: Required Associate’s Degree in the following field(s) of study: Business Administration, Marketing, Public Administration, Communications or relevant field. Two (2) years of experience in election work, public sector service, or relevant field. Travel required 5% - 25% May require KS/MO driver’s license, depending on department or agency. Johnson County Government requires reference/background screening for all positions. Specified criteria may vary by Department/Agency. Preferred Job Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in the following field(s) of study: Business Administration, Marketing, Public Administration, Communications or relevant field. Certified Elections Registration Administrator (CERA) Education may be substituted for experience. Experience may be substituted for education. Olathe, Kansas, United States

item.title: Government Services Legislative Intern
item.description: Summary: Barnes & Thornburg LLP is seeking a minimum of two (2) individuals to serve as Legislative Interns for its downtown Indianapolis office location. The interns will assist the partners and lobbyists in the firm’s Government Services Practice with activities related to the first legislative session of the 54th Indiana General Assembly. This competitively paid internship will begin January 4, 2027 and conclude on April 30, 2027. The internship will be a full-time (40 hours per week), on-site experience with regular participation in legislative activities at the Indiana State House and routine communication with firm clients at the direction of the intern’s supervisory attorney(s). Key Responsibilities: Each intern will be assigned to support one (1) or more partner(s) or attorney(s) throughout the duration of the legislative session. Such support will include assistance with drafting client communications, researching legislation and current statutes, and helping with client legislative events. Interns will routinely create and prepare client reports using customized legislative software ( training will be provided ) on legislation, amendments to legislation, and legislative hearings, the Indiana State Budget process, conference committees and other legislative matters. Each intern will assist in the preparation of a weekly legislative newsletter for clients and the creation of customized presentations for industry sectors and clients as directed by the intern’s supervising attorney. Interns will write legislative update reports, talking points, various communications, and alerts often under short deadlines/time constraints due to the pace of the legislative session. Monitor and track the progression of bills – including, but not limited to, in person attendance of committee hearings and events at the Indiana State Capitol. Assist clients in preparing for and participating in Day at the State House events and other legislative event activities. Assist with research and writing of legislative proposals. The employee must be able to perform all essential job duties and responsibilities of this position satisfactorily and as outlined, with or without reasonable accommodations. Reasonable accommodation requests may be accommodated, absent undue firm hardship. ​ Qualifications: Possess a bachelor’s degree or higher- level degree. Previous experience with the Indiana General Assembly will be preferred. Previous government or political background or government intern experience desired. Possess strong communication and public-speaking skills including the ability to communicate effectively with a diverse internal and external clientele or audience. Knowledge and understanding of state governmental processes. Be self-directed, proactive, and confident individual. Possess excellent time management, planning, organizational, team and interpersonal skills to respond to client requests on a regular and consistent basis. Working knowledge in Microsoft Office. Ability to work a minimum of 40 hours a week, including evening hours as necessary. This job description is intended to describe the general requirements of this position. As such, it is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of job duties or responsibilities required in this job. Subject to firm needs, duties and responsibilities of this position may change at any time, on a temporary or permanent basis, and with or without notice Working Conditions: Normal office environment with little exposure to excessive noise, dust, temperature and the like. The above is intended to describe the general content of and requirements for the performance of this job. It is not to be construed as an exhaustive statement of essential functions, responsibilities or requirements. Equal Employment and Opportunity Statement: Barnes & Thornburg is committed to equal employment opportunity in both principle and as a matter of policy. We will recruit, hire, train, promote, compensate and provide benefits to all applicants and employees without regard to ancestry, sex, race, color, ethnicity, national origin, gender, age, religion, religious creed, mental and/or physical disability, medical condition, military and/or veteran’s status, genetic information, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, or any other basis protected by applicable federal, state and local laws. This policy applies to all recruiting, hiring, promotions, upgrades, layoffs, compensation, benefits, terminations and all other privileges, terms and conditions of employment. The firm complies fully with all federal, state and local equal employment opportunity laws.

item.title: Registration Elections Supervisor
item.description: Pay Range: $57,125 - $91,971 Pay Grade: 19 Job Code: 29005 FLSA Status: Exempt Essential Functions: The following duties are normal for this position. The omission of specific statements of the duties does not exclude them from the classification if the work is similar, related, or a logical assignment for this classification. Other duties may be required and assigned. Supervises, directs, and evaluates assigned staff; develops and oversees employee work schedules to ensure adequate coverage and control; compiles and reviews timesheets; approves/processes employee concerns and problems and counsels or disciplines as appropriate; assists with or completes employee performance appraisals; directs work; acts as a liaison between employees and management; and trains staff in operations, policies, and procedures. Organizes, prioritizes, and assigns work; prioritizes and schedules work activities in order to meet objectives; ensures that subordinates have the proper resources needed to complete the assigned work; monitors status of work in progress and inspects completed work; consults with assigned staff to assist with complex/problem situations and provide technical expertise; provides progress and activity reports to ; and assists with the revision of procedure manuals as appropriate. Conducts elections; supervises personnel to ensure that all elections are conducted in accordance with state and federal laws and regulations; secures early voting locations and recommends schedule; appoints site managers and determines staffing requirements for early and election day voting; works with polling locations and County Information Technology staff to ensure technology capabilities; develops and reviews training for compliance with election laws; monitors early voting traffic; recommends changes in procedures to resolve issues; conducts election night precinct check in, election audit and preparation of precinct statistics; monitors election tasks lists; monitors election software programming; and oversees financial filings process. Implements, monitors and maintains registration functions and processes; reviews registration functions and processes such as felon registrations, duplicate voters, citizenship verification, jury summons questionnaires, provisional voting, election night precinct check in and election audit; monitors and ensures compliance with established protocols and procedures; and updates protocols and procedures as needed. Prepares and completes a variety of registration, production and election reports; compiles and/or tracks various administrative and/or statistical data; generates and prepares data; submits all mandated reports to local, state and federal regulatory agencies or others as required; and maintains related records. Maintains training and procedure manuals; and develops, updates, and revises manuals for all procedures involving voter registration and election functions. Interprets, applies, and ensures compliance with all applicable codes, laws, rules, regulations, standards, policies and procedures; initiates any actions necessary to correct deviations or violations; maintains a comprehensive, current knowledge of applicable laws/regulations and pending legislation that may impact department operations; and maintains an awareness of new products, methods, trends and advances in the profession. Assists in developing and implementing department budget; reviews budgetary needs and makes recommendations to the director; and monitors expenditures against approved budget. Minimum Qualifications: Associate degree in Public Administration, Business Administration or related field; five years of experience in elections or registration, to include lead or supervisory experience; or any equivalent combination of education, training, and experience which provides the requisite knowledge, skills, and abilities for this job. Specific License or Certification Required: Must possess and maintain a valid Georgia driver’s license; and possess and maintain, or attain with 6 months of employment, a State of Georgia GEOC Georgia Election Official Certification.

item.title: Registration Elections Coordinator
item.description: Description Pay Range: $46,441 - $74,769 Job Code: 29010 Pay Grade: 14 FLSA Status: Nonexempt Essential Functions: The following duties are normal for this position. The omission of specific statements of the duties does not exclude them from the classification if the work is similar, related, or a logical assignment for this classification. Other duties may be required and assigned. Leads and coordinates daily work activities of assigned staff; confers with supervisor to obtain direction regarding work assignments and priorities; organizes tasks in order to complete assigned work; monitors status of work in progress and inspects completed work; confers with co-workers, assists with complex/problem situations, and provides technical expertise; assists with training and instructing co-workers regarding operational procedures and proper use of equipment; and assists with supervision of co-workers by reporting employee problems and providing input on disciplinary action and employee performance evaluations. Enters new voter registration information; verifies accuracy and completeness of voter information; conducts research of state records; mails letters to retrieve missing information and documentation; updates existing records in statewide registration base; files new, updates existing, and pulls deleted voter registration cards as appropriate; scans and indexes registration and absentee applications; and files records and correspondence after processing. Recruits, interviews, hires, and trains poll officials and temporary workers; creates online training and curriculum for in-person training; writes and administers election procedures for poll workers; updates poll worker manual and other training materials; reserves training locations; creates poll worker training and election day schedules; and oversees printing and distribution of training materials. Monitors and manages County-wide master street files, district lines, and precinct maps; inputs new streets; makes corrections to streets placed in incorrect precincts; changes boundary lines if needed; maintains and draws congressional, house, senate, school board, and commission district lines for precincts; ensures accuracy of all district lines; redistricts, creates, and renames polling places; and creates precinct maps. Conducts site visits to ensure site is prepared for voting; checks voter identification; verifies voter information; assists and answers questions from voters; solves problems and resolves conflicts; ensures all necessary signage is in appropriate area of the polling site; prints election results and zero tapes for all advanced voting sites; completes Election Recap Sheet; and stores all absentee applications in boxes to send to the warehouse. Coordinates election activities; supervises early voting polls; requests equipment and supplies to fully operate early voting polls for each election cycle; issues paper ballots; manages balloting printer; verifies voters have received the correct ballot based on their registered address; inspects generated ballots for accurate dimensions; and performs all close-out duties. Maintains inventory of election equipment and office supplies needed to conduct day-to-day work activities. and updates and inventories election equipment after each election. Processes jury summons follow-up questions; processes name and address changes; and sends follow-up questionnaire if voter no longer resides in the County or state. Supplemental: We are looking for a highly motivated and detail-oriented individual to join our elections team in a fast-paced and highly regulated environment. The role demands a proactive individual who thrives under pressure and is committed to delivering exceptional results. Ability to work extended hours and during blackout periods as required during election cycles. Minimum Qualifications: Associate’s degree in Office Administration or a related field; two years of experience in elections, customer service, or office administration; or any equivalent combination of education, training, and experience which provides the requisite knowledge, skills, and abilities for this job. Specific License or Certification Required: Must possess and maintain a valid Georgia driver’s license.

item.title: Head Of Growth Business Development Sales Government Affairs Lykos
item.description: LOCATION Atlanta, GA / Washington, DC metro preferred. Travel 40–50%. ABOUT LYKOS Lykos is a U.S.-based advanced materials and manufacturing company building a qualification-led repair & sustainment network for defense and aerospace industries. Lykos is focused on enabling rapid repair and sustainment for critical systems through advanced materials manufacturing, distributed and modular capacity, and our secure data-layer. THE OPPORTUNITY In the role of Head of Growth you will build and lead business development, sales, and government affairs alongside our CEO and team of DoW liaisons. You'll own the path from first relationship to paid reorder. You'll also help shape the policy that makes distributed repair + sustainment repeatable across the Department of War. The position demands a candidate who has spent a career inside military and aerospace sustainment and acquisition. You know who actually makes the decisions: Product Support Managers, program offices, J4s, depot commanders, OEM aftermarket leaders, and Hill staff. You can walk our solutions from end to end, and you're ready to trade a big company for the chance to build something that matters. WHAT YOU'LL DO ● Build the growth function. Set strategy for BD, sales, capture, and government affairs, then hire and lead the team. ● Land initial proof points. Take the first OEM-authorized part family through qualification to point-of-need execution and paid reorders. ● Engage OEMs. Negotiate master agreements and field-of-use licenses allowing Lykos to repair and reproduce parts while OEMs retain design authority. ● Shape DoW demand. Partner with Product Support Managers, program offices, depots, and operational units to convert critical readiness items into funded programs. ● Leverage contracting vehicles. Utilize OTAs, public-private partnerships, SBIR/STTR, IBAS, and commercial OEM agreements. ● Lead government affairs. Build relationships on the Hill and across the executive branch to drive policies for distributed sustainment and qualification reciprocity. ● Manage pipeline and forecasting. Deliver win strategy, capture plans, proposals, and reliable revenue forecasts. ● Represent customer needs. Inform the product roadmap and platform development based on warfighter and OEM feedback. ● Support growth and strategy. Identify candidate facilities for acquisition and represent Lykos across key stakeholder meetings and industry events. WHO YOU ARE ● You have 10+ years in defense or aerospace business development, capture, government affairs, program management, or sustainment and logistics leadership. ● You've served in uniform, or held senior civilian or industry roles in DoW maintenance, logistics, or acquisition. You've seen readiness problems up close. ● You have deep, current relationships across DoW sustainment (AMC, NAVAIR/NAVSEA, AFSC, DLA, SOCOM, the organic depots) and OEM aftermarket organizations. ● You've personally closed and grown multi-million-dollar government or OEM contracts. ● You know the budget cycle (PPBE, POM, authorization and appropriations) and how a line item becomes revenue. ● You understand technical data rights, depot law, and how qualification and technical authority really work. ● You're technically comfortable. You can discuss cold spray, NDT, and FAA Part 145 with engineers, then brief a general officer in plain English. ● You're a builder. You've worked at or near an early-stage company, or launched a new business line inside a large one, and you want the ambiguity. ● You're a self-starter who writes your own white papers and isn't afraid to get your hands dirty. ● You like to win, and you laugh often. REQUIREMENTS ● U.S. citizen with an active Secret or Top Secret clearance, or the ability to obtain and maintain one ● Able to travel 40–50%of time ● Willing to register as a lobbyist under the Lobbying Disclosure Act if required ● Bachelor's degree; an advanced degree or senior service school is a plus NICE TO HAVE ● Experience in advanced manufacturing, additive, repair and overhaul, or aftermarket ● Experience sustaining unmanned systems or robotics (SOCOM, Army) ● Experience with M&A or integrating acquired businesses ● Exposure to commercial regulated industries such as FAA repair stations, energy, or rail ● Existing relationships with defense-focused VCs and primes

item.title: Legislative Analyst
item.description: Legislative Analyst Florida Legislature Tallahassee, Florida, United States Full-time 11 days ago $43,572 - $92,928 USD yearly General Summary This is work functioning as a technical expert to a legislative committee, legislators, and the public on the subject matter under the jurisdiction of the committee. Under close supervision of the staff director and committee members, the legislative analyst applies this expertise when researching and preparing staff analyses, reports, legislation, and amendments; responding to inquiries; and developing correspondence. Financial Disclosure: Pursuant to sections 112.3144 and 112.3145, F.S., this position is required to electronically file a Form 1 – Statement of Financial Interests with the Florida Commission on Ethics within 30 days of hire. Examples of Work Performed Analyzes and objectively summarizes proposed legislation to determine its effectiveness and the impact of its passage on the state and other entities and individuals. Researches and drafts legislation and amendments to legislation at the direction of the committee chair, committee members, and other legislators. Assists in planning full committee and/or subcommittee meetings to include agenda, speakers, presentations, and materials. Monitors the implementation of legislation in the Executive and Judicial Branches to ascertain that legislative intent is met. Briefs legislators verbally or in writing on issues to be discussed in committee, on the floor, or with constituents. Conceives, plans, and conducts research projects and performs legislatively mandated studies. Prepares oral and written reports on research and committee work such as end of session committee reports, interim projects, and oversight reports which include recommendations for legislative action. Provides information and problem-solving assistance to legislators, their constituents, and the public. Prepares letters, summaries, talk-sheets or speeches, reports, and informational memoranda on committee issues at the request of the committee chair, other legislators or staff director. Keeps abreast of new and ongoing issues affecting assigned area of responsibility by collecting resource materials, attending workshops and conferences, reading industry publications, communicating with agency personnel, and the public. Assists in the coordination of the work of the administrative assistant, legislative intern, and other staff members. Serves as liaison with state agencies. May operate a computer to perform word processing, database management, and/or spreadsheet applications. Performs other related duties as required. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Knowledge of legal terminology and legal research. Knowledge of applicable computer word processing, spreadsheet, and database programs. Knowledge of Florida state government, legislative rules, and procedures. Skill in reading comprehension, analysis, and organization. Ability to communicate effectively and concisely verbally and in writing. Ability to take action in situations which lack clear direction. Ability to take initiative on independent research projects. Ability to produce quality work under pressure. Ability to deal tactfully and courteously with the demands of Legislators, their staff, and the public. Ability to plan, organize, and coordinate work assignments. Ability to work cooperatively as a team member and to contribute to the efficient internal functioning of the committee staff. Ability to conduct in-depth, carefully documented and credible analysis under minimal supervision within established deadlines. Ability to conduct meetings and to make presentations. Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with others. Ability to work independently. Ability to collect and analyze data. Ability to organize data into logical formats for presentation in reports, documents, and other written materials. Ability to solve problems and make decisions. Ability to exercise discretion and confidentiality. Minimum Qualifications A bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university and three years of professional experience in research, analysis, program planning and evaluation, or administrative work. A master’s degree from an accredited college or university can substitute for one year of the required experience. A doctorate from an accredited college or university can substitute for two years of the required experience. Professional experience as described above can substitute on a year-for-year basis for the required college education. Salary Salary commensurate with experience. The Legislature offers a competitive benefits package. Application Deadline Open until filled. Submission of Application Interested parties may apply to GovernmentJobs.com. Accommodation for Disability If an accommodation is needed for a disability, please notify Human Resources at (850) 488-6803. Tallahassee, Florida, United States $43,572 - $92,928 USD yearly

item.description: Title: Spring 2027 Student Internship, Government Affairs Company : Tampa Electric Company Location: TECO Energy - Tallahassee State and City: Florida - Tallahassee Shift: Weekdays/Schedule Flexibility Where Your Education Meets Opportunity Are you a college student ready to gain real-world experience in your field of study? Candidates should have a basic understanding of the legislative process, have excellent research skills and strong verbal and written communications skills. This position is ideal for students pursuing a degree in Political Science, Public Policy, or a related field. Accountabilities: Support the Government Affairs team through a myriad of responsibilities including, but not limited to: • Assist in conducting research on issues, legislation or policy initiatives relevant to the company • Assist in the preparation of briefing materials, white papers and presentations for meetings and events • Attend governmental meetings, hearings, or other events and provide summaries or analysis of the proceedings • Assist with the tracking of legislation and public policy issues • Communicate and collaborate with team members and other stakeholders to achieve project goals • Participate in State & Regional Affairs meetings • Assist with organization of advocacy events and meetings • Assist in drafting correspondence and other written materials • Provide administrative support to the Government Affairs team Physical Location of Co-op Opportunities 106 East College Avenue, Suite 810, Tallahassee, Florida 32301 QUALIFICATIONS: Education: The successful applicant should be enrolled in an accredited university as a college undergraduate or a graduate level post-secondary educational program in a related discipline. Co-Op Requirements: • To qualify as a co-op student, enrollment in the university’s co-op program (proof of enrollment required); if not eligible for co-op program (or program unavailable), the student will be considered an intern. • A minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale is required. Preferred discipline or degree type: • Political Science • Public Polity • Business Year in School: • Junior or Senior Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities: • Strong interest in government affairs and policy making process • Strong research, writing and communications skills • Ability to work independently and as part of a team • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) Working Conditions • Normal office environment Preferred Availability: • 20-30 hours per week ideally but can likely accommodate up to 40 hours if that is what you are seeking. TECO Energy is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. #LI-SC1

item.title: Election Manager
item.description: Election Manager Seminole County Supervisor of Elections Office Sanford, Florida, United States Full-time 11 days ago $60,008 - $65,000 USD yearly Description The Election Manager is a key member of the Operations Department responsible for managing assigned election operations and maintaining year-round election readiness. Primary responsibilities include management of the election worker program; supervision of seasonal staff; election worker recruitment, training, scheduling and retention; administration of the election worker online portal; Early Voting and Election Day staffing; polling location readiness; and continuous improvement of assigned election processes. The Election Manager works closely with the Director of Operations and other departments while maintaining ownership and accountability for assigned programs. The position must anticipate operational needs, identify problems, develop practical solutions, and effectively manage multiple priorities and immovable election deadlines. Examples of Duties Election Functions Work with the Director of Operations to plan, coordinate, and execute assigned operational components of Early Voting, Election Day, and other election activities. Develop and maintain operational timelines, calendars, checklists, assignments, procedures, and deadlines. Monitor election preparations and proactively identify staffing, training, polling location, and operational concerns. Develop contingency plans for staffing shortages, polling location changes, and other assigned operational challenges. Coordinate assigned election night, audit, recount, post-election, and special election activities. Develop and maintain Standard Operating Procedures and documentation for assigned election operations. Coordinate with Logistics, Information Technology, Voter Services, Human Resources, and other departments as necessary to ensure operational readiness. Election Worker and Seasonal Staff Management Manage the election worker program from recruitment through post-election evaluation, including onboarding, scheduling, assignments, communication, performance tracking, payroll coordination, and retention. Recruit, supervise, schedule, train, coach, and evaluate seasonal support staff assigned to election operations, not specific to voter services, admin or information services areas. Maintain an adequate pool of qualified election workers and backup workers for Early Voting and Election Day. Manage election worker applications, qualifications, availability, assignments, training history, attendance, and required records. Identify and develop high-performing election workers for leadership positions, including Clerks and Assistant Clerks. Monitor staffing levels, cancellations, attendance, performance, and retention and proactively address identified concerns. Coordinate with Human Resources and Outreach regarding election worker onboarding, payroll, recruitment, and related workforce needs. Election Worker Training and Online Portal Manage the election worker training program, including curriculum, schedules, locations, instructors, online training, and classroom delivery. Develop and maintain position- specific training materials, manuals, presentations, quick-reference materials, exercises, videos, and assessments. Ensure training reflects current election laws, office procedures, accessibility requirements, voter service expectations, and lessons learned from previous elections. Serve as a lead trainer and prepare permanent and seasonal staff to deliver accurate and consistent election worker training. Monitor training registration, attendance, completion, assessments, and overall election worker preparedness. Serve as the primary operational administrator and business owner of the election worker online portal, including worker profiles, availability, assignments, training, resources, and communications. Evaluate training and portal effectiveness and coordinate improvements with staff, Information Technology, and vendors as appropriate. Early Voting, Election Day and Polling Location Readiness Develop staffing requirements using historical and anticipated turnout, election type, location activity, and other relevant information. Assign election workers to appropriate positions and locations and maintain adequate backup staffing plans. Monitor staffing throughout Early Voting and Election Day and coordinate replacement workers as necessary. Communicate operational instructions and location-specific information to Clerks, Assistant Clerks, and election workers. Support year-round readiness of Early Voting sites and Election Day polling locations, including site visits, accessibility, voter flow, parking, signage, and facility information. Assist with Election Day command center operations and resolve and document assigned election worker and polling location issues. Coordinate with Logistics and other departments regarding materials, equipment, transportation, polling location changes, and other operational requirements. Performance, Readiness and Continuous Improvement Maintain assigned election programs in a state of year-round readiness for scheduled, municipal, special, and countywide elections. Conduct post-election reviews using worker performance, staffing, training, incident, survey, and operational data to identify trends and opportunities for improvement. Develop and maintain meaningful performance measures for election worker recruitment, training, retention, preparedness, and performance. Track lessons learned, recurring issues, and corrective actions through completion. Update procedures, checklists, forms, training materials, workflows, and contingency plans based on operational experience. Research election practices, training methods, technology, and operational improvements used by other election offices. Monitor changes in election laws, rules, and procedures affecting assigned responsibilities and maintain appropriate records and documentation. Typical Qualifications Qualifications ( A comparable combination of education, training, and experience may be considered in lieu of the minimum qualifications. ) Must be a registered voter in the State of Florida. Must possess and maintain a valid Florida driver's license. Ability to lift and carry election materials and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds. Education and Experience Bachelor's degree preferred. At least three years of progressively responsible experience in operations, project management, workforce management, training, public administration, elections, or a related field preferred. Experience supervising employees, seasonal or temporary workers, volunteers, or large teams preferred. Experience developing or delivering employee or adult-learning training programs preferred. Experience managing complex projects involving multiple responsibilities, deadlines, and stakeholders preferred. Election or government experience preferred but not required. A comparable combination of education, training, management experience, and demonstrated operational ability may be considered. Skills and Abilities Strong leadership, management, organizational, project-management, and time-management skills. Ability to establish priorities, develop plans, and manage multiple responsibilities and immovable deadlines with minimal supervision. Strong decision-making, analytical, and problem-solving abilities, including the ability to anticipate problems and develop practical solutions. Excellent written, verbal, interpersonal, presentation, coaching, and instructional skills. Ability to develop effective training materials, procedures, workflows, calendars, checklists, reports, and operational documentation. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and ability to learn election software, online training platforms, workforce management systems, and other technology. Ability to remain professional, collaborative, flexible, accountable, and decisive under pressure. Ability to learn and maintain a working knowledge of federal and Florida election laws, administrative rules, and election procedures. Ability to supervise seasonal staff and effectively manage large numbers of election workers and simultaneous assignments. Ability to learn and administer election worker management, scheduling, online training, and workforce management systems. Ability to manage sensitive and confidential information appropriately and maintain political neutrality. Ability to lift and carry election materials and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds. Supplemental Information Preferred Knowledge Florida election laws and election administration. Early Voting, Election Day, and polling location operations. Seasonal or temporary workforce management. Adult-learning and employee training principles. Learning management, scheduling, employee portal, or workforce management systems. Payroll processes for seasonal or temporary employees. Project management, performance measurement, and process improvement. Working Conditions Work is performed in office and field environments with regular interaction with staff, election workers, polling locations, training facilities, vendors, and the public. Travel throughout Seminole County is required for training, polling location, Early Voting, and other election-related activities. Workload and schedule increase significantly during election cycles and require management of competing priorities and statutory deadlines. Must be willing and able to work extended hours, including early mornings, evenings, weekends, and holidays, sometimes with little advance notice. Must maintain the highest standards of professionalism, political neutrality, accuracy, confidentiality, accountability, and public service. Must respond effectively to unexpected staffing and operational issues during active elections. Flexibility to perform other assigned duties as necessary to meet the needs of the office. Mandatory Special Requirements Must be willing and ab
